Role: Project Director

Location: London, United Kingdom (2-3 days a week from Client offices in Slough/London)

About the role:

As Project Director, you will be accountable for Project Management, Resource Management and delivery operations. You will report to the Managing Partner and be a key member of the senior leadership team. You will define the governance, processes and standards that keep complex, high-volume, multi-channel programmes running smoothly. You will also build and develop a Project Management team that works with accountability, collaboration and a focus on continuous improvement. A central part of the role is leading change, including the practical adoption of AI and new technologies to improve efficiency, quality and speed. You will set the vision and step into the detail when it is needed, building confidence with senior client and internal stakeholders.

What you will be doing:

  • Lead and develop the Project Management and Operations teams, setting clear direction and expectations and creating a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.
  • Shape the team's structure and capabilities to meet the evolving needs of the business. Coach and mentor Project Managers and create clear routes for progression.
  • Be accountable for delivery standards across the account, so work is delivered on brief, on time and within agreed scope and commercial terms.
  • Define and embed project management methodologies, governance frameworks, SLAs, quality control processes and approval frameworks across all client workstreams.
  • Oversee end-to-end delivery of complex, high-volume programmes across social, digital, mobile, CRM, film, video and content production, from brief and scoping through to quality assurance and final delivery.
  • Act as the senior escalation point for complex delivery challenges. Identify risks and inefficiencies early and guide them through to resolution.
  • Set the operational framework for the Project Managers, including processes, systems, tools, playbooks, templates and standard operating procedures. Establish performance measures that show delivery health, team performance and resource utilisation.
  • Lead the Resource Management function with our global team, planning, forecasting and allocating talent so the right people and skills are on the right projects at the right time.
  • Be responsible for the commercial health of delivery operations. Establish costing models and financial controls, and ensure projects are scoped, costed and managed to support consistent, profitable delivery. Partner with Finance, HR and Recruitment to align resourcing and commercial objectives.
  • Manage external and offshore delivery partners so quality, cost and service expectations are consistently met.
  • Integrate AI and emerging technologies across project planning, workflow management, resource optimisation, reporting, quality assurance and content production. Set quality and governance standards, lead the rollout of new tools with measurable improvements, and build team confidence through experimentation and learning.
  • Build trusted relationships with senior client stakeholders as a credible partner on delivery, operational strategy and innovation. Work with Creative, Strategy, Production, Technology and Account Management leaders, and contribute to the senior leadership agenda that shapes the account's direction and growth.

What you need to be great in this role:

  • Experience leading Project Management and Resource teams at director or equivalent senior level within a creative, advertising, marketing or communications agency.
  • A track record of building, developing and coaching high-performing teams, including senior talent.
  • Expertise overseeing complex, multi-workstream programmes and delivering consistently against quality, time and commercial objectives.
  • Strong knowledge of integrated marketing communications, particularly social-first content, digital and always-on communications. This includes the demands of high-volume content, reactive opportunities, multiple formats, platform specifications and rapid approval cycles.
  • Experience designing, implementing and embedding operational processes, governance frameworks and project management methodologies, and leading systems implementation and adoption.
  • Commercial awareness, including forecasting, resource utilisation, project costing and profitability.
  • Experience managing offshore and nearshore teams, external partners and complex delivery models.
  • Experience working across creative, strategy, production, technology and account management functions.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence, constructively challenge and build credibility at senior levels.
  • Clear decision-making, with the ability to anticipate challenges, bring solutions rather than only escalate problems, and explain complex operational matters in plain terms.
  • A commitment to innovation and continuous improvement, with the organisation to manage competing priorities and attention to detail in a fast-moving environment.
  • Strategic integration of AI across studio projects and operations

Die Immobetriebe Hausverwaltung GmbH ist ein inhabergeführtes Unternehmen in Konstanz. Wir verwalten Wohnungseigentümergemeinschaften, Mietshäuser und größere Gewerbeobjekte im Raum Konstanz, Radolfzell und Singen. Wir arbeiten weitgehend digital: ein Vorgangssystem für alle Fälle, KI-Assistenz bei Routinen und Abläufe, die wir aufschreiben und gemeinsam verbessern.

Bisher haben unsere Verwalter die Umsetzung von Instandhaltung und Sanierung neben ihren rechtlichen Aufgaben mitgetragen. Diese Aufgabe lösen wir jetzt heraus und machen sie zu einer eigenen Stelle, die eng mit den Verwaltern zusammenarbeitet: Die Verwaltung führt Versammlung und Beschluss, Sie bringen die beschlossenen Maßnahmen auf die Baustelle und zum Abschluss.

Als Projektkoordinator sorgen Sie dafür, dass Instandhaltung und Sanierung in unseren Objekten zügig, in guter Qualität und im beschlossenen Budget umgesetzt werden. Die Ausführung liegt bei unseren Fachfirmen. Sie vertreten die Eigentümer als Bauherr: Sie planen, beauftragen, prüfen und halten nach, bis die Maßnahme abgenommen ist.

Aufgaben

  • Sie sehen sich Schäden und Instandhaltungsbedarf vor Ort an und schätzen ein, was zu tun ist und welche Gewerke gebraucht werden

  • Steht der Beschluss, setzen Sie die Maßnahme um: Sie beauftragen die Firmen, setzen Termine, koordinieren die Gewerke und halten nach, bis alles erledigt ist

  • Sie prüfen vor Ort, ob fachgerecht gearbeitet wird, nehmen Leistungen ab, verfolgen Mängel und prüfen Rechnungen gegen den Auftrag

  • Sie arbeiten im Rahmen der Budgets und Freigaben, die Beschlüsse und Verwaltervertrag vorgeben, und melden Abweichungen frühzeitig

  • Sie dokumentieren jedes Projekt im Vorgangssystem und erfassen Ihre Zeiten laufend

  • Ein großer Teil Ihrer Arbeit findet am Schreibtisch statt: Telefon, E-Mail, Angebote und Abstimmung mit Eigentümern, Beirat und Verwaltung

Qualifikation

  • Eine bautechnische Ausbildung, etwa im Handwerk, als Techniker oder ein Studium im Bauwesen, und mehrjährige Praxis am Bau oder in der Instandhaltung von Gebäuden

  • Ein gutes Auge für Qualität über mehrere Gewerke hinweg; Sie erkennen, was ein Schaden braucht und was ein Angebot taugt

  • Freude daran, Dinge zu Ende zu bringen und mehrere Maßnahmen gleichzeitig im Blick zu behalten

  • Verlässlichkeit im Umgang mit Budgets und Freigaben

title: Regional Sales Director, Core Enterprise – France
descriptionHtml:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role

Samsara is building its Core Enterprise business in France, and we are hiring a Regional Sales Director to lead it. This is a build role: you will create the market and the pipeline machine behind it, rather than inherit an established playbook.

You will lead a team of six Enterprise Account Executives. The team sells deals of €100K–€300K AOV over four to six month cycles, so the role calls for pace and velocity paired with value-based selling rigour.

In this role, you will

  • Own the performance, development and day-to-day leadership of a team of six Enterprise Account Executives
  • Build a pipeline machine and a market: define the target accounts, segments and motions that generate repeatable new business across France
  • Create and embed a team playbook covering prospecting, qualification, deal progression and handover, so the team sells consistently and new hires ramp quickly
  • Coach the team through each deal cycle, driving execution and velocity and embedding MEDDIC and Command of the Message
  • Pressure-test deal qualification, challenge assumptions, and help your team navigate the complexity of selling into large French enterprises. This isn't a role where you sit above the deals
  • Build the commercial muscles (cross-sell, multi-product attach, stakeholder mapping) that will drive durable growth as we expand our footprint across France's largest accounts
  • Run a structured operating rhythm of pipeline reviews, deal inspection and forecasting
  • Coordinate ADRs, Marketing, Solutions Engineering and partners around your team's priorities, influencing functions you do not directly own
  • Hire, develop and lead an inclusive, engaged and high-performing team, developing AEs into strong Core Enterprise sellers
  • Partner closely with your peer Regional Sales Directors, Samsara's wider leadership and Customer Success to ensure your team has the support it needs to win
  • Champion, role model and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and into new markets

Minimum requirements for the role

  • Three or more years of proven success leading new business sales at enterprise level, with a track record of revenue delivery and overachievement against target
  • Has built something rather than inherited it, with experience building a market or a new sales function from scratch
  • Full team lifecycle experience: has recruited, ramped and retained a team, and can show where each happened
  • Direct experience selling into enterprise companies at comparable deal sizes and cycle lengths
  • Experience establishing rigour in value-based selling, using methodologies such as MEDDIC or Command of the Message
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate supporting functions to drive pipeline and close business
  • Fluent French and access to our Paris office

An ideal candidate also has

  • Experience at a high-growth technology company, helping to build or refine the enterprise go-to-market playbook rather than inheriting an established one
  • A coaching-first leadership style, with a record of developing AEs from good to exceptional
  • Intelligence and genuine coachability: you learn fast, welcome feedback and apply it
  • A competitive, entrepreneurial streak: you create momentum without needing to own every function involved
  • Comfort operating in a fast-moving, scaling organisation where not everything is perfectly defined yet, and where you are expected to build process while delivering results
  • A blend of strategic thinking and tactical intensity: you can set the market strategy and also step into a deal review to show a rep where their qualification is weak

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you're ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. title: Regulatory Counsel
descriptionHtml:

Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. Eighteen of the top 20 global automakers, as well as the United States military and its allies, trust the company’s solutions to deliver physical intelligence. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in Washington, D.C.; San Diego; Ft. Walton Beach, Florida; Ann Arbor, Michigan; London; Stuttgart; Munich; Stockholm; Bangalore; Seoul; and Tokyo. Learn more at applied.co.

We are an in-office company, and our expectation is that full-time employees primarily work from their Applied Intuition office 5 days a week. However, we also recognize the importance of flexibility and trust our employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work, starting the day with morning meetings from home before heading to the office, or leaving earlier when needed to accommodate family commitments. This in-office expectation does not apply to contractor positions

About the role

We are looking for a Regulatory Counsel to join our Legal team to oversee global regulations governing physical AI and ensure comprehensive compliance across our growing product lines. You will serve as a regulatory advisor to many cross-functional teams, managing regulatory reporting and mitigating compliance risks in the rapidly evolving physical AI landscape.

 

At Applied Intuition, you will:

  • Analyze, interpret, and advise on global laws and regulations that affect physical AI and intelligent vehicles, including automated driving and ADAS rules (NHTSA, FMVSS, state AV frameworks, UNECE regulations, EU type approval), vehicle software and cybersecurity standards (UN R155/R156, ISO 21434, ISO 26262, SOTIF), AI governance laws (EU AI Act, US state AI laws), privacy and data access regimes, and related defense and export control requirements

  • Serve as a regulatory advisor to product, engineering, sales, and cross-functional teams, translating requirements into practical guidance and into the toolchain, Vehicle OS, and software development lifecycle

  • Draft and review comments on proposed regulations, written feedback on proposed legislation, responses to agency requests for information, and trade association submissions

  • Scope regulatory requirements for prospective partnerships, customer programs, and new markets, and support deal teams on regulatory terms in commercial agreements

  • Own regulatory reporting and agency filings, and build the internal processes and controls that keep them accurate and on time

  • Support responses to regulatory inquiries, audits, and information requests, in coordination with Public Policy, Security, Privacy, and outside counsel

We're looking for someone who has:

  • A J.D. from an accredited law school and active membership in good standing

  • 4 to 8 years of regulatory experience in-house, at a law firm, in government, or at a trade association, with substantive depth in administrative law, agency rulemaking, and compliance

  • Hands-on experience analyzing and drafting comments on proposed regulations or legislation

  • Experience advising on at least one of: vehicle safety regulation, autonomous vehicle or ADAS regulation, or export controls and defense compliance

  • The ability to explain complex legal requirements clearly to engineers, product managers, salespeople, and policy professionals, and to write memos and submissions that a regulator or legislator would find persuasive

  • Sound judgment in ambiguous situations, a practical and solutions-oriented approach, and the organization to run several matters at once under deadline

Nice to have:

  • Prior in-house experience at an autonomous vehicle (AV), OEM, or Tier 1 automotive supplier

  • A technical or engineering background to deeply understand autonomy product architecture and capabilities

Compensation at Applied Intuition for eligible roles includes base salary, equity, and benefits. Base salary is a single component of the total compensation package, which may also include equity in the form of options and/or restricted stock units, comprehensive health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance coverage, 401k retirement benefits with employer match, learning and wellness stipends, and paid time off. Note that benefits are subject to change and may vary based on jurisdiction of employment.

Applied Intuition pay ranges reflect the minimum and maximum intended target base salary for new hire salaries for the position. The actual base salary offered to a successful candidate will additionally be influenced by a variety of factors including experience, credentials & certifications, educational attainment, skill level requirements, interview performance, and the level and scope of the position.

We’re looking for an experienced, motivated Enterprise Account Executive to drive ElevenLabs’ growth across Healthcare: the health systems, hospitals, clinics, health plans, and life sciences companies people trust with their health and their families’ care. These organizations win or lose on trust and access at massive scale, under some of the most demanding regulatory standards anywhere.

  • Partner closely with Forward Deployed Engineers to solution high-impact use cases, manage a successful Proof of Value, scope integrations with the EHR, claims, and telephony systems customers already run, and set them up to scale in production

  • Partner closely with Legal teams to drive strategic, fast-moving negotiations, including BAAs

Requirements

  • 7+ years of quota-carrying enterprise sales experience in SaaS or technology, ideally with exposure to AI, generative AI, LLM-based products, or API-driven platforms

  • Healthcare experience (health systems, hospitals, payers, life sciences, health tech) is preferred but not required. We weigh demonstrated adaptability and fast ramp in a new industry heavily

  • Proven success closing six-and-seven figure deals and managing complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles

  • Proven ability to take a warm introduction through discovery, Proof of Value, and procurement to close

  • Experience selling to both technical buyers (IT, product, and engineering) and business buyers (patient access, operations, digital), and to privacy and compliance gatekeepers, translating complex technology into business value

An overview of this role

What you’ll bring

  • Comfort working both independently and as part of a distributed team, with attention to detail and alignment to GitLab’s values.
  • Openness to travel as needed and to apply transferable skills from related roles or industries in support of customer success and technical enablement.
  • Fluent French

About the team

The Customer Success Architect team focuses on hands-on technical enablement, adoption, utilization, and maturity of the GitLab DevSecOps platform while maintaining strong, consultative customer relationships and business alignment. You’ll work as part of a globally distributed, all-remote team that collaborates asynchronously with Customer Success Managers, Product Management, Engineering, Sales, Professional Services, and Support to act as a trusted advisor for customers. Our mission is to align GitLab capabilities with customer business outcomes, guide them along their adoption journey, and help them navigate complex technical and organizational change so they realize long-term value from GitLab. descriptionHtml:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

Core Platform builds the foundations every other team at ElevenLabs builds on: how users, workspaces and permissions work across our products. Our systems sit on the path of every request and are relied on by millions of users and by enterprise customers, so correctness, security and safe rollout matter as much as speed.

We are hiring full stack engineers (backend leaning) for two focus areas. Depending on the team you join, your responsibilities might include:

Workspaces & User Management (serving external customers)

  • Building and improving the building blocks customers touch directly: API keys, login experience, analytics, admin tooling, workspace security and more

  • Working closely with Sales, FDEs and customer teams to turn enterprise and self-serve feedback into the right improvements, and helping large customers with complex organisational structures.

  • Shipping customer-facing features end to end, from backend services to the admin and settings UI.

Permissions & Resources (serving ElevenLabs engineering teams)

  • Designing and building generic resource and permissioning services that product teams use to build features safely and quickly.

  • Solving hard, largely greenfield problems at scale, for example how a customer with a million agents assigns and manages access.

  • Working across product teams to understand their needs, and driving adoption with changes that don't require every team to rework their code.

In both teams you will:

  • Scope work as part of a large existing system: understand what exists, what could go wrong on rollout, whether a migration is needed, and how downstream teams are affected.

  • Roll out changes safely and with minimal disruption to existing users, teams or systems.

  • Debug and operate what you build, working from customer reports, logs and code.

  • Own features from scoping to completion, with the support of experienced engineers who are happy to mentor.

Requirements

We do not require any formal experience, certifications, or degrees. Instead, we are seeking engineers who can show they have solved impressively hard problems, through past projects or GitHub contributions. We do require:

  • Expertise in Python.

  • A strong background in backend development, with comfort working across the stack where the work needs it.

  • Experience with common software and system design patterns and infrastructure, including APIs, cloud infrastructure tools, storage solutions and data structures.

  • Strong test design and security fundamentals.

  • Care and attention to detail when changing live, business-critical systems, and the ability to learn a large existing codebase quickly.

  • Comfort with ambiguity: working out what should be built, and prioritising among competing signals.

Bonus:

  • Experience with authentication, authorization or permissioning (OAuth, SSO/SCIM, RBAC or similar).

  • Experience with Kubernetes.

  • Experience building internal platforms or services used by other engineering teams.

Location

Our team is based across the UK, EU and US, and this is our main focus. We are flexible for exceptional candidates elsewhere. You can work remotely, or from our offices in Dublin, London, New York, San Francisco and Warsaw.

descriptionHtml:

GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a Senior Backend Engineer on the Duo Chat team, focused on Chat Engine, you'll build the core AI capabilities behind GitLab Duo Chat, the natural-language and agentic interface to the GitLab DevSecOps platform. Much of your work will involve building flow components and agentic flows in the Flow Registry, the Python framework built on LangGraph within our Duo Workflow Service that powers agentic chat, and integrating them with the GitLab Rails monolith.

You'll own complex backend features from start to finish across both services. You'll integrate large language models and orchestrate multi-agent flows so customers can work faster and more securely across the software development lifecycle. This work sits where GitLab's core platform meets its AI strategy, and reliability, performance, and answer quality directly shape the customer experience.

What you’ll do

  • Design and build flow components and agentic flows in the Flow Registry using Python and LangGraph within the Duo Workflow Service. These reusable building blocks power agentic Duo Chat and, increasingly, other AI features across GitLab.
  • Develop, ship, and maintain backend features for GitLab Duo Chat across the Python Duo Workflow Service and the GitLab Rails monolith in a secure, well-tested, and performant way.
  • Integrate new generative AI models, providers, tools, and multi-agent orchestration patterns into Duo Chat to expand its capabilities and improve answer quality.
  • Design, implement, and review GraphQL and Representational State Transfer (REST) application programming interfaces (APIs) and related monolith logic, including chat entry points, permissions, and foundational-flow registration. Keep contracts with frontend clients and host systems reliable and clear.
  • Improve debugging, observability, and test coverage using pytest, RSpec, and related frameworks; track and improve latency, error rates, and test coverage so AI-powered chat workflows stay reliable at scale.
  • Collaborate with Product, User Experience (UX), frontend, and AI specialists to refine requirements and deliver high-quality improvements through iteration.
  • Document standards, patterns, and learnings with other engineers, raising the bar for safe AI integration and evidence-driven engineering.
  • Participate in Tier 2 on-call rotations to troubleshoot production issues, contribute to root cause analysis, and strengthen resiliency.
  • Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.

What you’ll bring

  • Significant experience building and maintaining production Python backends, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous or long-running workloads.
  • Practical experience designing and shipping AI-powered, agentic backend features, including large language model integration, tool or function calling, and multi-agent orchestration. You use sound judgment about large language model limitations and safe use in production.
  • Working proficiency in Ruby on Rails, or a strong willingness to learn it. Duo Chat integrates deeply with the GitLab monolith for chat entry points, GraphQL, permissions, and flow registration, and most of GitLab's codebase is written in Ruby.
  • Proficiency designing or extending REST or GraphQL APIs with attention to scalability, maintainability, and backward compatibility.
  • Strong Structured Query Language (SQL) skills and familiarity with relational databases such as PostgreSQL, including efficient queries and data modeling.
  • Ability to find, diagnose, and prevent performance and reliability problems at scale.
  • Experience solving technical problems of high scope and complexity and advocating for quality, security, and performance improvements across your team.
  • Openness to learning and collaborating in an async-first, distributed team, applying transferable skills from related technologies or domains. Hands-on experience with agent frameworks such as LangGraph or LangChain is a strong plus.

About the team

We're part of GitLab's AI Engineering organization and own the AI-powered chat experience embedded across the GitLab platform. Chat Engine is the backend-focused team within the Duo Chat group.

We're backend, frontend, and AI specialists working asynchronously across time zones, using issues, merge requests, and documentation as our main collaboration tools. Our focus is to expand generative and agentic AI capabilities, improve the performance and reliability of chat workflows, and strengthen the debugging and testing foundations that let us run AI features safely at scale.

  • Metric definitions, data requirements and acceptance criteria that engineering and systems teams can build against

title: Software Engineer - BrandX
descriptionHtml:
Olo is a leading SaaS platform accelerating digital transformation in the restaurant industry, by helping customers deliver more personalised and profitable guest experiences. As a result, our digital ordering, payment, loyalty and guest engagement solutions enable brands to do more with less and make every guest feel like a regular.

While our roots are in NYC, we’re intentionally investing in Belfast and Northern Ireland as a key hub, with an established leadership presence, a local team, and community for the long term. This role is fully remote, offering you flexibility to work from anywhere within NI.

Your new role

In this role, you’ll join as a Software Engineer on the ‘BrandX’ team, which is part of the wider ‘Order Engineering’ group.

BrandX (Brand Experience) builds the tools restaurant brands and Olo's internal teams use to run their business on Olo. We own the Dashboard that brand operators log into every day, the internal Admin application, and the billing and invoicing systems that turn platform usage into invoices. We also own how brands sign in and manage their users, including SSO and two-factor authentication, and we are building Olo AI Assist, a natural-language assistant inside the Dashboard.

The team is seven engineers spread across the US and Europe, and you'd be our first hire in Northern Ireland. Because the team sits between brands, Finance, and the rest of Order Engineering, the work is varied. One week you might be shipping a new Dashboard settings page, the next you're tracing a billing discrepancy across our finance integrations or teaching Olo AI Assist a new skill so a brand can update hours across hundreds of stores just by asking. You'll pair with senior engineers, review and ship code most days, and use Claude Code as a normal part of how you work.


How you’ll make an impact

  • Learn the BrandX domain and technology stack, and get to know the brands, Finance partners, and Order Engineering teams we work with.

  • Own small-to-medium features end to end, from understanding the requirement to shipping it, with senior engineers available when you need them.

  • Write code that meets our standards, and participate in code reviews as both author and reviewer.

  • Build reliable and maintainable software, with test coverage that matches the risk of the change.

  • Contribute to the team’s delivery pipeline, including test coverage, CI, and deployment practices.

  • Use Claude Code and GitHub Copilot as your default way of building, and help the team push what these tools can do.

  • Troubleshoot and debug production issues, learning how our systems fit together along the way.

  • Participate in team ceremonies such as daily stand-ups and retrospectives, sharing updates and feedback.

  • Take part in learning activities, including game days and training sessions, to build familiarity with Olo’s tools and processes.

  • Join the on-call rotation, with responsibilities that grow as you learn the team’s systems.


    • What will set you up for success

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • 1 to 3 years of professional software engineering experience, or a strong portfolio of shipped projects.

  • Working knowledge of C# and .NET, and comfort reading code you didn't write.

  • Some experience building web UIs. We use React and TypeScript, but any modern framework is a fine starting point.

  • Comfortable with SQL and relational data. A lot of our work is understanding how data moves between systems.

  • You understand the difference between unit, integration, and end-to-end tests and when each one earns its place.

  • AI coding agents are your default way of working. You use tools like Claude Code daily, you can explain the fundamentals underneath what they generate, and you're excited about a team that expects you to push them further.

  • You ask questions early, write things down, and are comfortable working with colleagues in other time zones.

    • About Olo

    Olo is a leading restaurant technology provider with ordering, payment, and guest engagement solutions that help brands increase orders, streamline operations, and improve the guest experience. Each day, Olo processes millions of orders on its open SaaS platform, gathering the right data from each touchpoint into a single source—so restaurants can better understand and better serve every guest on every channel, every time. Over 800 restaurant brands trust Olo and its network of more than 400 integration partners to innovate on behalf of the restaurant community, accelerating technology’s positive impact and creating a world where every restaurant guest feels like a regular. Learn more at olo.com.

title: Sr Data Platform Engineer

What you’ll need to be successful

  • 5+ years of relevant experience in Data Engineering / Data Platform Engineering / Data Architecture

  • Excellent analytical, written, and verbal communication skills, with a passion for continuous learning and teaching, and the ability to produce clear, precise documentation

title: UI Engineer (Based in CA or NC only)
descriptionHtml:
Mission: Live at the intersection of app runtime & security. Protect applications in a fundamental way so that developers can build great application services and not be constantly looking over their shoulder. BlueRock is changing the landscape of App runtime security.

The role

Location: Must be based in CA (preferably San Francisco Bay Area) or North Carolina

You will work alongside BlueRock's product designers and the control plane development team on our operator consoles. These are the React front ends that engineers and security teams use to manage large fleets of protected nodes, see what AI agents are actually doing across those fleets, and author the policy that constrains them.

The domain is AI and agentic systems, seen from the operations and security side. When an agent calls an MCP server, spawns a subagent, runs a shell command in a sandbox, or burns $40 of tokens in an afternoon, our UI is where a person sees it, understands it, and decides what to allow. So the interesting problems are visibility problems (how do you show a thousand agent sessions so someone can find the one that matters?) and control problems (how do you author an enforcement policy without a mistake taking production down?).

This is a mid-level role. We expect about 3–5 years of professional front-end experience, or equivalent work that clearly shows the same judgment. The ideal candidate is passionate about user experience, design, and AI-assisted software development, with a demonstrated grounding in engineering best practices. The title says UI, but the work doesn’t stop there: you’ll work closely with our backend services, and a feature is finished when it’s proven working live, not when the screen looks right.

Working with design delivered as code

At BlueRock, product designers design and collaborate in code. Instead of handing off static mockups, they build working UI with AI coding tools, against real data, and open merge requests. Iteration happens so quickly that it has outpaced our capacity for robust engineering collaboration and review.

This role closes that gap. You will collaborate directly with product designers and backend developers to keep UI development fast, by bridging the gap between vibe code and high-quality, sustainable, well-tested code. Some days that means reviewing and hardening a designer's branch so it can merge. Other days it means building the shared components, tests and guardrails that make the next branch need less hardening.

Beyond reviewing and hardening code, you'll help shape how it gets made. Working with designers and the AI tools they use, you'll turn what each review teaches us into shared components, conventions, tests and agent instructions. Over time the whole practice becomes more predictable, and each new branch arrives closer to production-ready.

Roles and collaboration

Software development roles are blurring more than ever. This role reports to product design, with API and data-layer guidance from our control plane engineering lead. You must be attuned to the perspectives of both UX/Design and Engineering, acting as a bridge between the goals and priorities of both sides, while ultimately deferring to UX/design partners on matters of style, copy, and information architecture.

In practice: when a designer's branch makes a choice about layout, copy or flow, you protect the intent and fix the implementation. When the implementation can't support the intent, because of performance, data shape or maintainability, you say so early and bring options rather than quietly changing the design.

What you'll do

  • Review designer-authored merge requests and bring them to production quality: structure, types, tests, accessibility, performance, and both light and dark themes.

  • Turn one-off UI from fast iteration into shared, documented components in our design system and Storybook, and migrate the apps onto them.

  • Make data-dense views hold up at real scale. Dashboards, tables, charts, and time-range and filter controls that work on a demo tenant also have to work on one with billions of events.

  • Wire UI to the API layer (GraphQL), and work with backend developers when a view needs a new query, field or endpoint.

  • Own UI test coverage: Vitest for units and Playwright for end-to-end flows, kept green in CI.

  • Test UI end to end in live, secured environments, with full authentication and authorization, real data and realistic load, before calling it done.

  • Keep UI work moving across release lines: shipping behind feature flags, and carrying fixes between branches when a release is frozen.

  • Fix UI bugs across the consoles and the Windows, Mac and Linux clients: layout and overflow, tooltips and popovers, empty and zero states, things that are technically correct and still confusing.

  • When needed, design new interfaces within the existing design system, and bring them to design for review.

  • Help set the guardrails that make AI-assisted UI development safe: lint rules, conventions, review checklists, and the instructions our AI coding tools follow.

How we expect you to work

These are the habits of a careful engineer. They matter more here, not less, because so much of the code you touch was drafted quickly by someone else or by an AI tool.

  1. Diagnose before you change. Find the actual cause, which is usually a layer away from the symptom, and be able to explain why your fix addresses it. A change that makes the symptom disappear is not the same as a fix.

  2. Small, deliberate diffs. Solve the problem in front of you. Don't refactor adjacent code on the way past, and don't build the abstraction you may need later.

  3. Fix it in one place. When the same bug shows up in three panels, the fix belongs in the shared component, not copied three times. Knowing where a change belongs is most of the skill.

  4. Verify, then claim. Run it, look at it, check both themes and a narrow viewport, get types and lint clean, and write the test where a test is what proves it. Then say plainly what you checked and what you did not. This applies double to AI-assisted work: you own the diff, whoever drafted it.

  5. Say when you're unsure. A requirement with two readings is a question, not a guess. Surfacing a problem early is always cheaper than discovering it in review.

Our UI stack and design system

Our front ends are several React and TypeScript apps that share one codebase: our enterprise operator consoles and our cloud product for builders.

All of them are built on our own design system. It is a shared React component library on top of Ant Design, with design tokens for color, type and spacing, light and dark themes, and a shared app shell for navigation, page layout and headers. Every component is documented in Storybook, published from CI, which serves as the reference for designers, engineers and AI coding tools alike. The library also carries written instructions for AI coding assistants, so generated code reaches for the system's components and tokens instead of inventing its own.

A large part of this role is the design system itself. That means promoting patterns out of individual apps into shared components, writing their stories, keeping tokens and themes consistent so the apps don't drift, and making the system the easiest path for anyone, or any agent, building UI.

  • Front end: React, TypeScript, Vite

  • Design system: our component library built on Ant Design, including design tokens and light and dark themes

  • Documentation: Storybook, published to GitLab Pages

  • Data and charts: GraphQL; ECharts for the data-dense views

  • Testing: Vitest, Playwright, and contract and smoke suites in CI

  • Delivery: GitLab merge requests and pipelines, release branches, feature flags

  • Further back: TypeScript and Rust services over graph and columnar stores, built on OpenTelemetry, plus desktop apps and services across Mac, Windows and Linux

You don't need experience with all of it. You do need to be strong in TypeScript and React, and willing to read code before changing it.

What you bring

  • About 3–5 years building production front ends in TypeScript and modern React: hooks, composition, state that lives at the right level, and an understanding of why a re-render happens.

  • An end-to-end view of the systems behind the UI. Designing in code gets a feature most of the way to working, and you close the rest of the gap. For you, “done” doesn’t stop at the UI working. It means the UI is integrated and shown to work live, in a secured environment with full authentication and authorization, under realistic load.

  • Integration testing against complex backends. Tests that only run against mock data in a standalone dev stack aren’t enough here. You can create, integrate and run tests in live environments to check data validity, load, security and scale, and you keep unit, integration and end-to-end suites green in CI.

  • Performance instincts for data-heavy UI: pagination, virtualization, server-side filtering, and knowing when a slow page is a query problem rather than a rendering problem.

  • A track record of reviewing other people’s code and improving it without rewriting it.

  • Git in complex repositories with several active release branches, where a single fix may need to be cherry-picked, ported or graft-merged onto more than one of them. Readable commits, and responding to review without taking it personally.

  • Hands-on use of AI coding tools in real work, with clear habits for checking what they produce.

  • CSS that holds up: flexbox and grid, overflow and scroll containers, responsive behaviour, and why a tooltip or popover ends up clipped.

  • Experience building or contributing to a component library or design system, ideally with Storybook and design tokens.

  • Careful attention to visual detail and real interest in UX. Much of this work is noticing that something is two pixels wrong, or that a label is technically correct and still confusing.

  • Genuine interest in the AI and agentic space, and in the operational and security questions it creates.

Nice to have: Ant Design; GraphQL; ECharts or other charting libraries; design training or a portfolio; experience on a team where designers commit code; writing conventions or instructions for AI coding tools; desktop UI across Mac, Windows and Linux; dense operational tooling such as observability, security or infrastructure products.

Not required: a computer science degree, if your work shows the same rigor. Deep backend, security or infrastructure expertise, or any knowledge of our domain (fleet management, telemetry, agent observability, policy enforcement). We will teach that.

Your first 90 days

  1. First month: land changes safely. Ship scoped fixes in the consoles. Learn the component library, theme tokens and API layer. Start reviewing designer merge requests alongside an engineer.

  2. Second month: own review on a surface. Become the primary reviewer for designer-authored UI on one product area, and extract at least one repeated pattern into a shared component.

  3. Third month: make the next branch easier. Get the flows you own covered by tests in CI, and write down the conventions and guardrails that make designer branches need less hardening.

About BlueRock:

BlueRock is a well-funded, early stage cybersecurity company founded by experienced security minded entrepreneurs. Our mission is to change the game in cybersecurity. Attackers are exploiting in hours. The dependency tree is exploding. Developers are drowning in vulnerability debt. BlueRock changes the game, enabling organizations to shift from chasing CVEs and exploits to proactively protecting the foundations of applications and computing, so that developers can build great applications without looking over their shoulders.

title: Robotics Application Engineer
descriptionHtml:
At Rhoda AI, we’re building the next generation of generalist intelligent robots. We own the full robotics stack from high-performance hardware and robot systems to the infrastructure and state-of-the-art foundation world models that control our robots. Our robots are designed to be generalists capable of operating in complex, real-world environments and handling long-tail edge cases, made possible by our cutting edge research and end-to-end system design. We've raised over $450M and are investing aggressively in model research, infrastructure, hardware development, and manufacturing scale-up to make generalist robotics a reality.

Robotics Application Engineer – Rhoda AI GmbH (Germany)

About Rhoda AI GmbH
Rhoda AI GmbH is Rhoda AI's first international entity, established to own strategic partner relationships across Europe and drive deployment of Robotics as a Service (RaaS). It's a small, high-ownership team: you'll work with the Managing Director and Commercial Lead as peers from day one, with a direct line to our engineering organization in Silicon Valley.

About the Application Engineering Team
Application Engineering is where Rhoda's AI meets the real world. We work directly with customers and strategic partners to understand their operational problems, determine where our platform can deliver value, and lead the application of Rhoda's AI model end to end — from model post-training and data collection, to robot tooling and work-cell design, to production deployments on the customer's floor. The team sits at the intersection of engineering, product, deployment operations, and business, with members in the US and Germany. Application Engineering is organized into three complementary roles — Application Engineers, Solution Engineers, and Technical Program Managers.

The Role
As a Robotics Application Engineer, you are a core member of Rhoda AI's European team and the hands-on technical lead in the early stages of a partner engagement — Scoping, Proof of Principle (POP), and Proof of Concept (POC) — through to RaaS deployment. You'll determine whether a use case is feasible, design and prototype the end effectors and task tooling a robot needs to do the job, write the data collection procedures that feed our models, and post-train Rhoda's AI model to perform the task. You'll spend real time on partner sites across Europe standing up POCs and showing what our platform can do.

You'll also serve as a key technical bridge between our European partners and Rhoda HQ Engineering, owning the feedback loop that turns field findings into product improvements.

What You'll Do

  • Scope new partner use cases alongside the commercial team: ask the right questions, assess technical feasibility, and make go/no-go recommendations.

  • Design, prototype, and iterate on end effectors and task-specific tooling for real-world manipulation tasks.

  • Author and refine data collection SOPs, and work with teleoperation and ML ops teams to gather high-quality training data.

  • Post-train and evaluate Rhoda's AI model on partner tasks, driving performance toward POC success criteria.

  • Lead on-site POP/POC setup and execution, including model training, daily reporting, validation, and direct partner interaction, and author the final technical report.

  • Partner with Solution Engineers on task engineering and solution design input as engagements move toward production.

  • Review proposals and provide technical feedback ahead of purchase orders.

  • Support model training through Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), deployment, and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT).

  • Lead root cause analysis for issues surfaced during deployments, troubleshooting across hardware, firmware, and software until the real cause is found.

  • Share field learnings with product and engineering in Silicon Valley, translating partner-reported issues into prioritized, actionable input for the roadmap.

  • Present clear, non-technical summaries of technical outcomes to partner leadership, and work with the commercial team to tie them to commercial milestones.

What You'll Bring

  • BS or MS in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, Computer Science, or a related field.

  • 3–8 years of hands-on experience in robotics, automation, systems integration, or applied engineering in an industrial setting, including real-world deployments or field installations.

  • Strong mechanical design skills, including CAD (e.g., SolidWorks, Onshape, Fusion) and rapid prototyping (3D printing, machining, off-the-shelf components).

  • Working knowledge of machine learning workflows — data collection, training, and evaluation — and comfort working in Python.

  • Experience with robot arms, grippers, and sensors (cameras, depth sensors, LiDAR, IMUs) in real environments, including integration and calibration.

  • Proven track record conducting root cause analysis on complex systems spanning hardware, firmware, and software.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and comfort working with ambiguity in high-stakes environments.

  • Clear communicator who can explain technical tradeoffs to partners, executives, and internal teams. Fluent English required; German at working level minimum.

  • Willingness to travel approximately 40% across Europe, including extended on-site POC periods, with occasional travel to the US.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with imitation learning, VLA models, world models, or robot foundation models.

  • Background in factory automation, material handling, or logistics.

  • Experience in a customer-facing technical role (application, field, FDE, or sales engineering) at a robotics OEM, system integrator, or corporate automation department.

  • Familiarity with teleoperation systems or remote robot management workflows.

  • Experience with ROS/ROS2, embedded Linux, or C/Rust for onboard software.

Why Rhoda AI GmbH

  • Work on real customer problems, not lab demos: our robots are ready for field deployment directly after a successful POC.

  • Direct line to HQ Engineering — your field intelligence shapes the product roadmap.

  • Small, high-ownership team where you work with the Managing Director and Commercial Lead as peers from day one.

Love to Give Back

title: Safer Gambling Analyst
descriptionHtml:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Our mission is to create the safest and greatest online gaming experience and our dedicated team of executives are at the forefront of identifying and interacting with our customers to educate and inform on how to remain safe whilst enjoying our sites.

YOU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR:

WHO WE ARE

At the core of LeoVegas Group is Team Leo. Our culture is our foundation and is what enables us to innovate, build, and lead as we trailblaze our way through the igaming industry. We’re a team of over 2000 innovators, initiators, and groundbreakers working in a fast-paced and agile environment across 19 offices worldwide.

  • A social culture you’ll love – Regular opportunities to attend sporting events throughout the year, plus a quarterly team budget for even more fun.

  • Support for growing families – Up to 6 months of full pay for maternity leave.

  • Stay active & save money – Cycle-to-work scheme and gym discounts to keep you moving.

  • Work in style – at our newly renovated offices at Tailors Corner are just a 2-minute walk from Leeds Train Station.

  • And there’s more… We’ll share even more perks related to your role when you chat with our Talent Acquisition team!

In our pride, we empower our teammates to find their roar and run with their wildest ideas. We don’t wait for things to happen; we pounce and make it happen!

title: Sales Development Representative
descriptionHtml:
About Us

Tebi is creating the first Connected Restaurant Management System that makes hospitality flow. In one seamless platform, Tebi embeds sales, reservations, kitchen prep, payments, and all the data that powers it, creating smooth service and intuitive insights.

Founded by Arnout Schuijff, co-founder of Adyen, and backed by €50 million in funding from Index Ventures & CapitalG, Tebi is built in service of hospitality first. Thousands of restaurants, cafés, bars, and coffee shops across the Netherlands, UK, and more countries soon, love running on Tebi.

About the Role

We're looking for a highly driven SDR to join our team. You’ll be at the heart of our growth engine - managing the beginning of our sales cycle, directly driving our business and revenue growth by bringing in new customers.

In this role, you’ll blend your people and communication skills with passion to make hospitality businesses more smooth in their operations. You will act as the first point of contact for the customer, working collaboratively with internal departments to ensure we are not just winning business, but building long-term value and market share.

What You’ll Do

  • Own top of the funnel activity for a dedicated region.

  • Hit conversion targets across the stages of the funnel that are in your responsibility.

  • Communicate our value and mission to our prospective partners, build trusted relationships with the hospitality network in the region.

  • Do market research and competition analysis to identify opportunities within your region.

  • Collaborate with Ops, Product, and Leadership to remove bottlenecks and improve scaling.

  • Ensure smooth handoff to Success following close to drive activation and ongoing performance.

  • Maintain high CRM hygiene to enable the best handover to the sales and success team.

What You’ll Need

  • 0-1 years of experience in Sales, Sales Operations or Customer-facing roles ideally within SaaS/ Tech/ Hospitality or Startup space.

  • Passion for the hospitality industry and customer-facing activities is a strong plus.

  • Bachelor's degree in business, finance, engineering, or a related field (or equivalent work experience) is a strong plus.

  • Willingness to roll up your sleeves and “Leave your ego at the door” mentality

  • Self-motivated with the ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced startup environment.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to effectively engage with customers and internal stakeholders.

  • Entrepreneurial mindset: you thrive in fast-moving environments, love building from scratch, and bias toward action.

  • The ideal candidate will be fluent in English and Dutch

If this speaks to you we can be the right fit. Learn more about how we work from our Recipe here: https://www.tebi.com/gb/careers.

Benefits:

  • Start-up Equity

  • Competitive Salary

  • Lunch Provided in Office

  • Team events

What is Restaurant Software?

Restaurants and other merchants use various software systems such as Point of Sale (POS), Reservations, Kitchen Display Systems (KDS), Payments, Inventory, Staffing, and the list goes on. These systems all need to speak to each other which they frequently don’t. It’s a mess, and we are fixing it.

From buying a croissant at a cafe to having dinner with friends, it’s a €4 Trillion+ global market and a critical part of everyday life in today's economy.

How we use AI at Tebi

We use AI the way our merchants use Tebi, to cut out the friction and get to what matters faster. We believe in a world where AI increases quality, efficiency and speed.

At Tebi, AI isn't a policy or a checkbox, it's just part of how we work. It helps us write, analyse, build, and improve but doesn’t make the last call. If there's a smarter way to do something, we want to find it.

title: Sales Manager - Mid Market

Sales Manager - Mid Market

London

 

Wordsmith

Legal touches everything that matters in a business: every deal, every hire, every launch, every risk. Sales runs on Salesforce. Engineering runs on GitHub. In-house legal runs on inboxes, chat threads and tools that weren’t built for it.
Wordsmith is changing that. We’re building the platform in-house legal runs on.

Requests from across the business come in through one front door. AI agents handle the routine work. Lawyers stay in control where judgment matters. Legal finally gets to triage by risk, not by whoever shouted loudest.

We’re built for in-house teams, not law firms. Our customers want to spend less on outside counsel, not more, and we’re on their side of that equation.

More than 500 companies run on Wordsmith, including Financial Times, Canva, Trip.com, Revolut, Adyen, Trustpilot, and Sage. We’ve raised $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe and others, and we’re growing fast.

We're hiring a Sales Manager to lead and scale our Mid-Market UK&I team.

You'll own the number for your team, coach a group of full-cycle Account Executives, and build the processes that help them succeed. Your focus will be hiring, developing people, and driving consistent team performance.

This is an early-stage environment. Things move fast, priorities shift, and there isn't always a clear playbook. You'll need to make decisions, set the standard, and keep your team focused and moving.

  • Coach the team on building relationships with Legal Ops leaders, General Counsel, and Heads of Legal

  • Work closely with Product and Marketing to sharpen messaging and improve conversion

What we're looking for

  • Strong in discovery, demo, and value-led selling, and able to teach it

  • Comfortable selling into complex organisations and senior stakeholders

  • High ownership; you take responsibility for outcomes, not just activity

  • Organised, consistent, and reliable with strong follow-through

 

How we work

We're an in-office team. We work together because it makes us faster, sharper, and more effective. You should expect to be in the office as your default.

This is a high performance environment. We set a high bar, move quickly, and expect people to take ownership of real problems.

There isn't always a clear path. The people who do well here figure things out, stay close to the work, and keep pushing until they get to the right outcome.

This won't suit everyone. If you're looking for a highly structured environment or clear boundaries around pace, this likely isn't the right fit.

Why Wordsmith

We're in a period of strong momentum, growing quickly, winning new customers, and expanding into larger accounts.

The product is landing well, the market is ready, and the team is scaling to meet demand.

If you want to build a team, develop great salespeople, and grow quickly in a high bar environment, this is one of the best places to do it.

title: Security engineer, detection and response (UK)
descriptionHtml:
🚀 About WRITER

WRITER is the AI platform built for the world’s most ambitious marketing and revenue teams, bringing the frontier of AI to the people who drive enterprise growth. With WRITER, autonomous agents work across the buyer journey, continuously executing on market signals and enterprise intelligence to grow revenue faster. Every agent action and asset is grounded in trust, built on an Enterprise Brain that unites brand, product, and company knowledge with fiduciary-grade governance and compliance.

Fortune 500 companies are transforming how they go to market with WRITER, including 3 of the top 5 US banks, 2 of the 5 largest global CPG conglomerates, and 4 of the top 5 US healthcare insurers. Founded in 2020, WRITER is backed by investors including Insight Partners, ICONIQ, Radical Ventures, Premji Invest, Balderton, B Capital, Salesforce Ventures, Adobe Ventures, Accenture, Citi Ventures, IBM Ventures, WndrCo, and others. Learn more at WRITER.com.

📐 About the role

Join WRITER's security team as a staff detection and response engineer and help protect the AI infrastructure that's transforming how the world works. You'll build sophisticated detection systems that identify attacks targeting our AI platform, training data, and model deployments while creating automated response capabilities that scale with our explosive growth. This isn't just traditional security work – you're defending cutting-edge AI/AGI systems against adversaries who are evolving their tactics as fast as AI itself advances.

This role combines hands-on security engineering with strategic thinking to stay ahead of novel threats that don't exist in textbooks yet. You'll be the operational arm of our security function, translating threat intelligence into real-time detections, coordinating incident response across multiple teams, and hunting for sophisticated attacks across GPU clusters and distributed training environments. If you're excited by the challenge of securing systems that are fundamentally different from anything you've protected before, this is your opportunity to define what AI security engineering looks like at scale.

You'll work closely with our AI Security research team, Cloud Infrastructure, Software Security Engineering, and AI researchers to build a defense-in-depth strategy that protects one of the most valuable AI platforms in the industry. The threats are real, the stakes are high, and the problems are intellectually fascinating.

This role can be based inSan reporting to our head of security operations.

🦸🏻‍♀️ What you’ll do

  • Design and implement detection strategies that identify AI-specific threats including prompt injection, model extraction, data poisoning, adversarial examples, and unauthorized access to training datasets or model weights across our distributed infrastructure

  • Build automated response playbooks and orchestration workflows that contain threats without human intervention, creating self-healing security systems that reduce mean time to response from hours to minutes while automatically remediating compromised inference endpoints

  • Lead security incident response coordination across all teams (Cloud, AppSec, Enterprise, AI Security) when AI infrastructure or models are compromised, conducting forensic investigations on training pipeline attacks and model manipulation attempts while drafting clear incident communications for engineering and executive leadership

  • Hunt proactively for sophisticated threats across GPU clusters and training infrastructure by analyzing model outputs for signs of compromise, reproducing AI-specific vulnerabilities from security research, and identifying visibility gaps in distributed training environments before adversaries exploit them

  • Build detection-as-code frameworks with version control and automated deployment, onboard telemetry from AI training infrastructure and inference endpoints, and create dashboards that track model security metrics, GPU utilization patterns, and access to sensitive research data

  • Collaborate cross-functionally as the operational security partner for all teams – translating AI Security's threat research into production detections, monitoring Cloud Infrastructure's GPU clusters for threats, detecting customer-impacting incidents for Software Security Engineering, and enabling responsible AI development through security guardrails

  • Maintain 24/7 on-call rotation for critical AI security incidents, responding to real-time threats targeting our platform while continuously improving detection coverage and automation capabilities as our AI systems evolve

⭐️ What you need

  • 3-5+ years in security operations, detection engineering, or incident response with a proven track record of identifying and stopping sophisticated attacks in production environments, plus 3+ years specifically securing AI/ML infrastructure, high-performance computing environments, or other distributed systems at scale

  • Strong programming skills in Python, KQL, SPL, or similar languages that allow you to build custom detection logic, automate response workflows, and create tools that operationalize security at scale across cloud-native and distributed computing environments

  • Experience with SIEM platforms, detection technologies, and forensic investigation techniques with demonstrated ability to build detection for novel attack techniques that don't have established patterns yet and to conduct forensics in complex distributed environments

  • Self-directed execution mindset with a track record of securing high-value intellectual property, automating incident response in complex environments, and identifying critical security gaps through proactive threat hunting before they become incidents

  • Deep alignment with WRITER's values – you naturally Connect across security, infrastructure, and AI research teams to build comprehensive defenses, you Challenge assumptions about what's possible in AI security engineering, and you Own the protection of our AI platform with unwavering accountability and a commitment to staying ahead of evolving threats

title: Security Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About Boltz

Boltz is a public benefit company building the next generation of AI-powered molecular modeling tools to make biology programmable and accelerate drug discovery, while keeping frontier capabilities broadly accessible.

Boltz was founded by former MIT scientists who created Boltz-1, the first fully commercially available open-source model to approach AlphaFold 3-level accuracy in predicting the 3D structure of biomolecular complexes.

We focus on two things:

  • Foundation models. Our open models, Boltz-1, Boltz-2 and BoltzGen, are trusted by 100,000+ scientists across biotech and academia, and used in programs at every Top 20 pharma as well as leading agrichemical and industrial research organizations. Our latest proprietary foundation models power our products and the custom models we build with partners.

  • Boltz Lab and the Boltz API. Our products run our latest models, design pipelines (BoltzMol for small molecules, BoltzProt for protein design) and agents as reliable, production-grade tools built around real chemistry and biology workflows. Teams start from a target and a hypothesis, then generate, evaluate, and rank candidate molecules in Boltz Lab, run our models from their own code and agents through the Boltz API, or deploy them inside their own environment.

The two feed each other: our open releases earn scientific credibility and community insight, and our products turn our full range of models into real impact for partners including Pfizer, Takeda, GSK, Bristol Myers Squibb and DSM-Firmenich.

You can read more about our mission, research and product vision in our manifesto.

About the role

Our partners trust us with their most valuable secrets: unpublished targets, novel molecules and years of proprietary assay data. Your job is to make sure that trust is well placed, everywhere our platform runs: our own cloud, dedicated single-tenant environments, and partners' own AWS and Google Cloud accounts.

You will be a founding engineer on our security team, part of the Platform team in Core Engineering, shaping the security program with our CTO, who leads it today. You will work with every engineering team at Boltz, and you will sit across the table from the security leaders of the world's largest pharma companies.

We want security to be the reason a partner says yes faster, not the reason a deal stalls. This role is ideal for a hands-on engineer who would rather fix a control in code than write a document about it, and who can explain risk clearly to a pharma CISO.

What you'll do

  • Make secure the default: build guardrails into our Terraform, Kubernetes and CI/CD so every new cluster, environment and partner deployment inherits the right boundaries from day one.

  • Protect what matters most: keep partner data isolated across tenants and deployments, protect our model weights, and make sure the agents acting on scientists' behalf can only do what they should.

  • Make the secure path the easy path: identity, secrets, service-to-service authentication and supply-chain controls that engineers actually want to use.

  • See and stop threats: logging, detection and incident response across AWS and GCP, with exercises that keep us sharp.

  • Find weaknesses first: threat-model new features before they ship, run penetration tests, and attack our own agents and APIs before anyone else does.

  • Turn trust into an advantage: lead security reviews with partners' security teams, translate their requirements into engineering work early, and run our SOC 2 Type II program and the frameworks partners ask for next (e.g. ISO 27001) with evidence generated by our systems, not by screenshots.

  • Secure the company: identity, device management, access reviews and security awareness for a small, highly technical team.

This role is not a compliance-only (GRC) or SOC analyst role. Most of your time goes into engineering; compliance should be a by-product of controls that actually work.

About you

Minimum Requirements

  • 4+ years of security engineering experience in cloud-native SaaS or infrastructure companies.

  • Deep, hands-on cloud security experience on AWS or Google Cloud: IAM and multi-account or multi-project organizations, network security, encryption and key management, audit logging and threat detection.

  • Infrastructure-as-code (Terraform) and enough hands-on engineering to ship security improvements yourself.

  • Application security experience: threat modeling, secure code review, authentication and authorization (SSO, OAuth/OIDC, MFA), web and API vulnerabilities.

  • Experience owning a SOC 2 or ISO 27001 program through an external audit, or building the controls one depends on.

  • Practical incident response experience.

  • Low ego, high ownership, and pragmatic trade-offs between risk and speed; clear with engineers, leadership and partners' security teams alike.

Preferred Requirements

  • Kubernetes and container security (network policy, admission control, workload identity, image signing).

  • Security for ML or LLM systems: agent tool access, prompt injection, model and training-data protection.

  • Experience as an early or founding security hire at a startup.

  • Securing deployments in customer-controlled, multi-cloud or regulated environments.

  • Exposure to life-sciences or pharma security and data-protection expectations (e.g. GDPR).

  • Offensive security or penetration testing background.

We know great people don't always tick every box. If this role excites you and you meet most of the minimum requirements, we'd like to hear from you.

What we offer

  • Shape the security program that lets the world's leading pharma companies trust frontier AI with their discovery programs.

  • Work alongside one of the most talent-dense teams in the field.

  • Significant ownership and independence, with responsibility for driving projects from concept to deployment.

  • Highly competitive salary with meaningful equity in a public benefit company.

  • Benefits:

    • 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays

    • Annual team offsite trip

    • Private healthcare (BUPA), covering pre-existing conditions

    • Pension program

    • Paid parental leave

    • Wellhub gym membership

    • Free lunch every day

    • Travel expenses

How we hire

  1. Initial screen with a member of the Talent team

  2. Security design and threat-modeling interview

  3. Onsite in London or virtual onsite with the team

  4. Offer + Onboarding

Our commitment

Boltz is committed to building a diverse team and an inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds. If you need any adjustments during the hiring process, tell us and we'll make it work.

  • Mobilize a large matrix virtual team of business stakeholders to include Operations, Finance, IT, dedicated Solution Engineer and Account Development Representative

If you want to shape how the workforce wins in the AI era, come and join us.

The AI Transformation team

AI Transformation is a small, focused squad that is driving Multiverse’s next wave of growth. Our mandate is to rebuild how the company actually works, function by function, and to establish the practices that make Multiverse an AI-first company from the core out.

But our work doesn’t stop there. We are building a product that we will take to market to truly be a transformation partner to our customers. Joining this team means shaping the future of Multiverse, of our customers, and of the wider workforce as we navigate the new world of work.

Influence technical direction. You have opinions about how things should be built, and you back them up with evidence. You contribute to architectural decisions, push back when the team is heading in the wrong direction, and propose better approaches.

descriptionHtml:
TEAMWFP ist eine Agentur für kreatives VkF-Marketing in Mönchengladbach.
