title: Social Media & Campaign Manager
descriptionHtml:
Über Cell Labs

Wir bauen humanoide Systeme: Full Stack, von Hardware und Elektronik über Software bis zur Fertigung, alles in-house in Berlin.

Bei Cell Labs verschieben wir die Grenze dessen, was Robotik leisten kann. Unser Ziel ist klar: Systeme bauen, die Menschen stärken statt sie zu ersetzen. Unsere Technologie ist bereits bei führenden Industriekunden und Partnern im Einsatz. Jetzt steht unser eigenes Produkt kurz vor dem Launch.

Die leise Phase ist vorbei. Wir suchen Menschen, die früh dabei sein wollen, Verantwortung übernehmen und das bauen, worüber andere nur reden.

Ort: Berlin · Start: Ab sofort · Arbeitsmodell: Vor Ort · Anstellung: Vollzeit

Deine Aufgaben

  • Content-Produktion: Du produzierst Shorts, Reels und Posts für LinkedIn, Instagram und YouTube, vor und hinter der Kamera. Vom ersten Konzept über den Dreh bis zum fertigen Schnitt.

  • Social-Media-Redaktion: Du verantwortest unseren Redaktionsplan und entscheidest, welches Thema auf welchem Kanal läuft. Du machst aus einem Engineering-Fortschritt einen LinkedIn-Post, aus einem Testlauf ein Video und aus einem Meilenstein einen Moment, über den geredet wird.

  • Community Management: Du sichtest Kommentare und Nachrichten, antwortest im Tagesgeschäft und erkennst, wann ein Thema an das Team oder die Gründer:innen geflaggt werden muss.

  • Kampagnen & Launch: Du setzt Kampagnen operativ um, insbesondere die Kommunikation rund um unseren Produktlaunch: von Teasern über Content vor Ort bis zum Recap. Mit Creator:innen und Partnern arbeitest du dabei eng zusammen.

  • Founder-Content: Du recherchierst Themen und schreibst Entwürfe für LinkedIn-Beiträge, die unsere Gründer:innen aus ihrer eigenen Perspektive veröffentlichen.

  • Du entwickelst eigene Formate aus unserem Material: Unser Videograf kümmert sich um Dokumentation und aufwendige Produktionen. Du machst daraus eigene Formate, schneidest Snippets und organisierst kleinere Drehs selbst.

  • Reporting: Du misst Reichweite, Engagement und Profilbesuche, wertest aus, was funktioniert, und bringst die Erkenntnisse in den nächsten Redaktionsplan ein.

  • Brand Consistency: Gemeinsam mit unserem Brand & Communications Lead bringst du unsere Markenstrategie in die tägliche Content-Arbeit. Du sorgst dafür, dass unsere Marke über alle Kanäle hinweg wiedererkennbar bleibt.

Das bringst Du mit

  • Erfahrung: Mindestens zwei Jahre im Social Media Management oder in der Content Creation, in einer Agentur, einem Startup, einem In-house-Team oder als Freelancer:in. Du hast mindestens eine Kampagne eigenständig umgesetzt und kannst zeigen, was dabei herauskam.

  • Vor und hinter der Kamera: Du stehst gerne selbst vor der Kamera und drehst und schneidest Shorts eigenständig, zum Beispiel in Premiere, CapCut oder DaVinci Resolve.

  • Redaktion und Konzept: Du denkst in Formaten und Serien, schreibst gute Texte und weißt, wie sich ein Thema auf LinkedIn, Instagram und YouTube jeweils anders erzählt.

  • Produktion: Kleinere Drehs organisierst du selbst, von der Location über das Equipment bis zur Abstimmung mit allen Beteiligten.

  • Neugier: Interesse an komplexen Technologien und die Motivation, tief in die Robotik einzutauchen und technische Zusammenhänge verständlich zu machen.

  • Zahlen: Du kennst die Analytics der Plattformen und leitest daraus ab, was du als Nächstes anders machst.

  • Sprachen: Deutsch und Englisch fließend.

Das bieten wir Dir

  • Deine Arbeit ist das, was die Welt von uns sieht: Feeds, Launch, Event. Fast alles, was die Öffentlichkeit von unseren Robotern mitbekommt, geht über deinen Tisch.

  • Alles unter einem Dach: Büro, Werkstatt und Teststände liegen im selben Gebäude in Kreuzberg. Wenn du den Roboter in Aktion filmen willst, ist der Engineer ein paar Schritte entfernt, ganz ohne Ticket.

  • Room to Fail & Grow: Bezahlte Lernzeit mit persönlichem Budget für Kurse, Konferenzen und die Tools, die du brauchst. Du bekommst Raum, neue Formate auszuprobieren, und begleitest einen Launch, den bisher kaum jemand gesehen hat.

  • Benefits: Ein Leistungspaket, das du dir selbst zusammenstellst und das Mobilität, Gesundheit, Ernährung oder Fitness abdeckt. Dazu gibt’s einen zusätzlichen bezahlten freien Tag im Jahr für ehrenamtliches Engagement oder ein Projekt, das dir am Herzen liegt.

Bewerbung

Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf und Links zu Content, den du selbst produziert hast, idealerweise eine Kampagne oder Serie, die du von der Idee bis zur Veröffentlichung umgesetzt hast. Dazu ein paar Zeilen: Was war das Ziel, was hast du gemacht, was kam dabei heraus? Ein Anschreiben brauchen wir nicht.

Der Prozess: Intro Call, Deep Dive in deine bisherige Arbeit, Besuch bei uns mit einer kleinen Content-Aufgabe, Angebot.

Wir bauen Roboter für alle, deshalb wollen wir ein Team, das das abbildet. Wir stellen nach Fähigkeiten ein und freuen uns ausdrücklich über Bewerbungen von Menschen, die in Social Media und Tech unterrepräsentiert sind. Wenn du nicht jeden Punkt erfüllst, aber denkst, das ist dein Job: bewirb dich.

title: Software Engineer (Data)
descriptionHtml:
Our Mission

We’re not your average benefits platform – we’re the driving force that uplifts people’s lives. Our technology connects the entire benefits ecosystem, creating better outcomes for employers, employees, brokers, and providers.

Our mission is clear: to build a world where everything works at its best, ensuring every employee gets the support they need to thrive—both at work and beyond.

Your Mission

As our Software Engineer (Data), you’ll build and run the pipelines, orchestration, and infrastructure that move data across Ben: in from our product and the tools we use, in from our customers, and back out to them again. It’s the plumbing the whole company and our customers depend on, and it has to stay reliable. We serve global enterprise customers with strict security and reliability requirements.

You’ll own real work from day one. You’ll have a strong team of cross functional engineers alongside you, room to grow into harder problems, and the freedom to do the job your way.

What you’ll be working on

  • Own everything that flows into Ben: build and maintain the ingestion pipelines that bring data into our warehouse, with Fivetran for managed sources and custom pipelines where we need them.

  • Keep everything running on time: own the orchestration that keeps data moving on schedule and recovers cleanly when something breaks.

  • Scale and manage our data infrastructure: build and manage our data infrastructure as code with Terraform, using mainly AWS services.

  • Connect Ben to every system our customers run: build enterprise-grade pipelines and connectors for our customers, bringing their data in, for example from HR and payroll systems, and getting accurate data back out to them, reliably and securely, even at the volumes large customers bring.

  • Build the data layer our agents act on: help connect our data to the AI agents and services we're building, including through MCP connectors, so they get the right context at the right time.

  • Shape what we build: work with product and other stakeholders to scope problems and agree on simple but scalable solutions.

  • Build it to enterprise standard: build to current security practice, for example the OWASP Top 10 and the AWS Well-Architected Framework.

Behind the scenes

Ben runs on Python 3, Django, PostgreSQL, and React, on AWS.

Our data platform today is built around Fivetran, AWS DMS or custom pipelines for ingestion, dbt for transformation, PostgreSQL on AWS RDS as the warehouse, and n8n or AWS Lambda for automation between systems. We manage our infrastructure as code with Terraform and use different AWS services depending on requirements.

We have adopted frontier level agentic development practices and continue to push the envelope of what’s possible with current technologies.

Your skills and experience

  • Strong experience with Python and SQL.

  • A few years building and running production data pipelines that other people relied on.

  • Comfortable with infrastructure as code, ideally Terraform, and hands-on with AWS, for example Lambda, ECS, Glue, S3, RDS.

  • A good grasp of ETL/ELT and orchestration.

  • Experience building or running data integrations and connectors, especially ones that other companies or customers depend on, is a real plus.

  • Solid software engineering fundamentals: clean code, sensible design, and tests you can rely on.

  • You keep security in mind when you build applications and configure infrastructure, and you know what enterprise customers expect of their data.

Nice to have, not essential:

  • Experience working on customer-facing data integrations such as HRIS or payroll feeds via SFTP and in EDI format

  • Experience with MCP server development, or different ways of preparing data for AI agents such as ontology modelling, context, knowledge graphs, and semantic layers.

We don't expect all of it. We do expect curiosity about it.

Why join us?

Ben's customers are large enterprise employers, and the hundreds of thousands of people who work for them rely on us to get their benefits right, every time. That depends on data moving accurately between their systems and ours, every cycle. You get to work on the data infrastructure that makes this run like clockwork.

At the same time, Ben is an AI-native organisation. Agents are already doing a lot of impactful work here, and they can only do it on data they can trust. That raises questions a dashboard never had to answer. How fresh does this need to be for an agent to act on it? How do you match the same entity across tools? How do you control what an agent is allowed to see? Very few engineers have answered those in production. You'd be one of them.

You'll take ownership of large, complex problem spaces, help design how they scale, and build an agentic layer few engineers have built anywhere yet, and you'll see the impact of it: Ben supports hundreds of thousands of people across 30+ countries.

Our Compensation & Benefits

It's important to us to practise what we preach when it comes to benefits. We know what good looks like and we want to provide the best for our team, with a comprehensive and inclusive benefits package. You'll have a choice over the things that are most important to you. You can see a selection below, with the full offering here.

💰 Competitive base salary + equity, so you own what you build

⭐ Bonus scheme designed to reward and recognise high performance

💳 £100 monthly personal Ben Balance: for whatever works for you, whether that's Netflix, Spotify, or a really expensive cup of coffee! This allowance will increase by £50 for each year of service until you reach £250

🍔 Weekly lunch provided in office so you can spend quality time with the team over some tasty food!

🏖 28 days of holidays a year plus bank holidays, and an option to buy or sell 2 days per year. Your holiday entitlement increases to 30 days at your 3rd year of service!

🌴 Work-from-abroad scheme, so you can support your travels, enjoy an extended holiday, or visit loved ones.

🍼 Enhanced parental leave and workplace nursery scheme to support with the cost of childcare in a nursery setting

❤️ Comprehensive Private Medical Insurance

💌 Funded Life Assurance cover with the option to voluntarily increase. This also includes an annual health check

 

Diversity and Culture at Ben

We are organically growing a brilliantly diverse, inclusive and respectful bunch of people we are extremely proud of. This should go without saying, but all applications are very much welcome. TULIP was founded out of the MIT Media Lab. It is headquartered in Boston, has offices in Munich, Tokyo, Tel Aviv, Budapest and Singapore, and has customer sites in more than 45 countries.

In January 2026, TULIP closed its $120M Series D, at a valuation of $1.3B. Leading global manufacturers run on TULIP, including VEKA, DMG Mori, Roche, AstraZeneca, Richemont, Saint-Gobain Aerospace and Mitsubishi Electric. TULIP is part of the World Economic Forum's Global Innovator community, and our CEO, Dr. Natan Linder, co-chairs the Forum's Advanced Manufacturing Industry Governors Community. 

The opportunity in DACH for TULIP

DACH is the heart of global manufacturing. Germany is Europe's largest industrial economy and the birthplace of Industrie 4.0. Switzerland is a global centre for pharma, life sciences and precision manufacturing. Austria is a strong base in automotive, machinery, metals and semiconductors. The region is also home to many of the world's "Hidden Champions", mid-sized companies that lead global niche markets. title: Special Projects Manager
descriptionHtml:
About Zego 🚀

At Zego, we're on a mission to do the good thing, not the insurance thing.

Insurance hasn't changed much in over a century. The way we live, work and travel has. We're building the real-time, AI-driven infrastructure that powers innovative insurance, so good drivers get cover that works the way they actually drive.

We're not just updating insurance; We're leading the AI evolution in insurance 🤖

For us, AI isn't a line on a roadmap or a buzzword on a slide. It's our operating reality, and it's how we build products that back drivers instead of the old insurance playbook.

We don't do things slowly, and we don't do bureaucracy. We back high-performance builders who want ownership, early responsibility and the chance to do the most career-defining work of their lives. You'll get the space to try things, the tools to move fast, and the room to see your ideas reach millions of drivers.

Do not take our word for it. Read what Zegons say about us on Glassdoor.

If you're ready to build the future of insurance, we're hiring.

About the role

Reports to Zego's Deputy CEO.

This role exists to take on the problems that don't fit anywhere else. No two quarters will look the same. One might be launching a new product line. The next, building the framework and analysis that decides where we invest. Then designing an AI system that replaces a manual process, taking over a business unit and running it, leading a cross functional programme nobody else can unblock, or building the story we take to shareholders, investors and the Board.

It's the fastest way to understand how a leading AI company actually works: tech, product, marketing, operations, finance, regulation. You'll work directly with the people who run each of them.

What you will be doing

  • Whole problems, not work-streams. You take something ambiguous, scope it, build the plan, win the buy-in, deliver it, then either hand it over or run it. Launching a new product. Rebuilding a revenue line that has stalled. Standing up a capability from nothing.

  • Decisions worth making. You'll use quantitative and qualitative evidence to work out what's really going on, then make the call and defend it in front of the leadership team. Analysis that doesn't impact a decision isn't the job.

  • AI that does real work. You'll design and build AI systems and workflows that take work off people's plates, in content, analysis, operations or reporting. We expect you to reach for AI first, and to be the person others copy.

  • The narrative. Company wide updates, investor material, Board packs. You'll turn complicated business reality into something a smart outsider can follow in ten minutes.

What you will need to be successful

  • Proof you've done something hard. A business you built, a product you launched, a number you moved, a broken thing you fixed. We care about what happened, not what you were responsible for.

  • Real AI fluency. You've built your own tools, agents or workflows, not just used a chatbot. Come ready to show us.

  • Speed with judgement. You've worked somewhere genuinely fast, most likely a high growth startup, strategy consulting or similar and you know the difference between impact and effort.

  • Comfort with numbers and with people. You can build the model, then sit with an underwriter, a regulator or a shareholder and be taken seriously in both rooms.

  • Ownership as an instinct. Nobody will hand you a brief, a template or a team. You'll find the work, prioritise it and finish it.

  • Communication that lands. Clear writing, clear slides, clear thinking, in front of any audience from an engineer to the Board.

  • You work AI-first. You will use AI daily here, and we mean daily. You do not need to arrive an expert, but you do need to arrive curious, experiment fast, and take ownership of getting good quickly. People who wait to be trained will find this uncomfortable.

The Zego ways of working 🏡

Teams work better with time to collaborate and space to get things done. We call it Zego Hybrid: some of us are in our office (central London, Gibraltar or Halifax) weekly, others monthly or quarterly. It's about finding the balance between face time and focus that produces great work and a healthy life around it.

We also make a point of getting everyone in the same room. Teams come together every quarter, and once a year the whole company does, properly. It's a serious investment and consistently one of the best parts of the year.

Here is what the last one looked like.

Benefits 🎁

💰 Market-competitive salary, benchmarked against your function and reviewed every year.

🏆 Annual performance bonus, linked to company performance and your contribution.

📈 Share options, a real stake in the company and a share in the future you build

🩺 Private medical insurance.

🏖️ Pension, generous holiday, and £1,000 a year to spend on getting to the office or learning something new.

💻 Cutting-edge systems and tools, so you always have what you need to drive your impact.

Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? We want to hear from you.

Zego, leading the AI evolution in insurance.

Who You Are:

  • Proven Experience: 10+ years of experience in product management, solution architecture, technical consulting, CTO/CPO role.

We're at the beginning of a new era in customer experience, one where AI doesn't just respond, but understands, reasons, and takes action. We're building agentic AI that enterprises trust with their most important customer moments: complex questions, high volumes, real stakes. When millions of people reach out to a brand, those interactions aren't just support tickets; they're defining experiences. title: Staff Product Engineer, AI

Together with Salesforce, the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success, we're building the future of customer experience. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. Ready to level up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You're in the right place. Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

What's the opportunity? 

We’re looking for Staff Product Engineers to join the AI Group to build Fin's AI-powered products. Product Engineers working in ML work closely with both our ML Scientists and product teams. They must deeply understand our product, our customers, our ML tech stack and our broader product stack. 

Our group is responsible for defining new ML features, researching appropriate algorithms and technologies, and rapidly getting first prototypes in our customers’ hands.

We are an extremely product focussed team. We work in partnership with Product and Design functions of teams we support. Our team's dedicated Engineers enable us to move to production fast, often shipping to beta in weeks after a successful offline test.

We are very passionate about applying machine learning technology, and have productized everything from classic supervised models, to cutting-edge unsupervised clustering algorithms, to novel applications of transformer neural networks. We test and measure the real customer impact of each model we deploy.

If you are an experienced product engineer who takes an analytical approach to development and has some hands-on experience with ML systems, we'd love to hear from you! 

What will I be doing? 

Product Engineers in the AI Group

  • Build the systems that power Fin's flagship AI products. This usually means working in our ML Python tech stack, but at times also means working across the product on our Rails app too.
  • Work alongside our ML Scientists bring proof-of-concept code to production; ensuring it’s robust and scalable for real-world use.
  • Partner with product teams outside of our group, to shape the best AI-powered product experience for our customers..
  • Contribute to all phases of software development including ideation, prototyping, and implementation and testing.
  • Play an active role in the hiring, mentoring, and career development of other engineers.
  • Raise the bar for technical standards, performance, reliability, and operational excellence within the group and across Fin.

Profile we’re looking for 

These are meant to be indicative, not hard requirements.

  • 10+ years of experience shipping high-quality products.

  • Strong willingness to fight for good outcomes

Bonus skills & attributes 

  • Previous experience in data analytics, or statistical role

title: Staff Software Engineer - Workloads
descriptionHtml:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.   We're proud to be a Living Wage accredited Employer.

About the Team

Launchables is CoreWeave's platform for building Physical Intelligence. We bring simulation, training and evaluation tools into a common platform, allowing robotics, autonomous systems and engineering teams to focus on their applications while Launchables handles common execution and infrastructure needs.

We turn specialist Physical AI software into capabilities that researchers and engineers can use, adapt and build upon. Our work combines strong software engineering with applied domain knowledge to make complex workloads accessible, reproducible and useful in real-world environments.

As a Staff Software Engineer, Workloads - Physical AI, you will develop engine integrations, application code, adapters, templates and developer tools that make specialist software available through Launchables. You will work directly with researchers and engineers to understand their tasks, assumptions, dependencies and expected outcomes, translating these into interfaces and configurations that preserve the capabilities they need.

You will take ownership of how users configure, run, customise and evaluate workloads. This includes defining meaningful inputs, defaults, constraints and outputs; building command-line and API interfaces; and creating examples and documentation that help users extend existing templates or author their own. You will establish appropriate validation for packaging, execution and application outcomes, working with domain specialists to make evaluation criteria and their limitations clear.

You will profile workloads to improve preparation time, GPU utilisation, concurrency and data movement while preserving the intended computation. You will also capture the inputs, versions, settings and execution conditions needed to reproduce runs, with logs, metrics and artefacts that help users diagnose failures, compare experiments and interpret results.

Working alongside engineers responsible for the shared runtime and platform services, you will turn feedback from early users into better interfaces, defaults, tests and guidance. You will identify reusable patterns across integrations, shape shared platform capabilities, review designs and mentor colleagues. You will use coding agents and automation to accelerate development, applying the review, testing and domain judgement needed to ensure the resulting software behaves as intended.

Qualifications:

  • Strong software engineering skills, demonstrated through dependable software or developer tools used by other people.
  • Applied depth in at least one relevant area, such as robotics simulation, autonomous-vehicle evaluation, reinforcement learning, synthetic-data generation or engineering simulation.
  • Experience making specialist or research software usable beyond its original author, including configuration, testing, documentation and diagnosis.
  • Sound judgement about experimental assumptions, evaluation criteria, reproducibility and the conclusions a result supports.
  • Familiarity with containerised execution and experience tracing problems across application and infrastructure boundaries.
  • Comfortable learning unfamiliar tools and domains, working closely with specialists and recognising when their expertise is needed.
  • Evidence of improving shared tools or engineering practices across multiple projects, with clear reasoning about what should be common and what should remain application-specific.

Preferred Skills:

  • Experience developing software in Python, Go or C++.
  • Familiarity with simulation and machine-learning frameworks.
  • Experience profiling GPU workloads and identifying performance or resource bottlenecks.
  • Experience with Kubernetes or workflow orchestration.

Wondering if you're a good fit?

We believe in investing in our people, and value candidates who can bring their own diversified experiences to our teams - even if you aren't a 100% skill or experience match. Here are a few qualities we've found compatible with our team. If some of this describes you, we'd love to talk.

  • You enjoy turning specialist Physical AI software into dependable tools that other researchers and engineers can use independently.
  • You care about making experiments understandable and reproducible, with clear evidence of what their results do and do not establish.
  • You combine hands-on engineering with curiosity about unfamiliar domains, and enjoy helping colleagues build reusable, high-quality systems.

We welcome relevant experience from industry, research engineering and academia. We are interested in what you have built, how others use it and the judgement you brought to making it work.

Why CoreWeave?

At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast! We're in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. We're not afraid of a little chaos, and we're constantly learning. Our team cares deeply about how we build our product and how we work together, which is represented through our core values:

  • Be Curious at Your Core
  • Act Like an Owner
  • Empower Employees
  • Deliver Best-in-Class Client Experiences
  • Achieve More Together

We support and encourage an entrepreneurial outlook and independent thinking. We foster an environment that encourages collaboration and enables the development of innovative solutions to complex problems. As we get set for takeoff, the organization's growth opportunities are constantly expanding. You will be surrounded by some of the best talent in the industry, who will want to learn from you, too. Come join us!

The base salary range for this role is £116,000 to £155,000. The starting salary will be determined by job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and the market location. We strive for both market alignment and internal equity when determining compensation. In addition to base salary, our total rewards package includes a discretionary bonus, equity awards, and a comprehensive benefits program (all based on eligibility).

To fulfill our obligation to protect client data, successful applicants offered employment with CoreWeave will be required to complete a basic criminal record check, conducted in compliance with GDPR. Employment offers are conditional upon receiving satisfactory check results.

Ensemble, nous visons à créer des histoires pleines de sens ainsi que des concepts de produit liés au monde et aux attributs emblématiques de Karl. Le prêt à porter pour femme, les sacs, la petite maroquinerie et les sous-vêtements sont gérés directement depuis notre siège d’Amsterdam, tandis que d’autres catégories, incluant le prêt à porter pour homme, les parfums, la lunetterie et autres, sont développés avec les meilleurs partenaires de licence de leur catégorie. Basée à Berlin, Q ENERGY Solutions est une société sœur de Q CELLS, fabricant de modules photovoltaïques reconnu à travers le monde. title: Stagiair HBO Logistiek/ Supply chain
descriptionHtml:
STAGIAIR HBO LOGISTIEK / SUPPLY CHAIN
32-40 uur

Wil jij jouw analytische talent inzetten voor logistieke vraagstukken met directe impact? Bij BERG hebben we meerdere stageplekken binnen Logistiek & Supply Chain. Je werkt aan een concrete opdracht waarmee je onze logistieke processen verder professionaliseert en krijgt volop ruimte om jouw eigen ideeën en oplossingen te ontwikkelen.

Of je nu enthousiast wordt van logistieke optimalisatie en containerbelading of juist van transportdata, benchmarking en dashboards: bij BERG is er ruimte voor jouw talent.

Create your future
Als stagiair(e) Logistiek & Supply Chain werk je bij BERG aan een logistiek vraagstuk met directe impact op onze internationale supply chain. We hebben meerdere stageplekken, waarbij je afhankelijk van jouw interesse aan de slag gaat met één van onze twee opdrachten.

Interesse in logistieke optimalisatie? Dan ontwikkel je een Container Load & Capacity Optimizer. Je onderzoekt hoe we onze containerruimte beter kunnen benutten en ontwikkelt op basis van onder andere SKU’s, afmetingen, gewichten en laadrestricties een praktische tool die de optimale belading en benodigde capaciteit berekent.

Ligt jouw interesse meer bij transport, data en dashboards? Dan ontwikkel je een Transport Benchmark & Selectie Dashboard. Je analyseert offertes van pakket- en palletvervoerders en maakt tarieven, toeslagen, gewichtsklassen, landen en serviceniveaus inzichtelijk. Met scenarioanalyses en een dashboard help je BERG om transporteurs beter te vergelijken en besparingsmogelijkheden te ontdekken.

Bij beide opdrachten werk je met data, Excel en mogelijk AI en is er volop ruimte voor jouw eigen ideeën. Je werkt samen met logistieke collega’s en zorgt ervoor dat jouw oplossing niet alleen goed werkt, maar ook daadwerkelijk binnen BERG gebruikt kan worden.

100% you
Voor beide stageopdrachten zoeken we studenten die analytisch sterk zijn en graag een complex logistiek vraagstuk vertalen naar een praktische oplossing.

• Je volgt een hbo-opleiding in Logistiek, Supply Chain Management, Technische Bedrijfskunde of een vergelijkbare richting.
• Je hebt sterk analytisch en wiskundig inzicht.
• Je werkt nauwkeurig, gestructureerd, kritisch en zelfstandig.
• Je vindt het leuk om data te analyseren en hiermee tot concrete oplossingen te komen.
• Je hebt affiniteit met Excel, data-analyse, dashboards en/of AI-toepassingen.
• Je bent praktisch en bedrijfsmatig ingesteld en betrekt gebruikers actief bij jouw oplossing.

What’s in it for you?
Je krijgt de kans om mee te werken aan concrete logistieke vraagstukken binnen een internationaal merk en oplossingen te ontwikkelen die écht gebruikt worden binnen BERG. Je draait mee met ervaren logistieke collega’s en krijgt zo de kans om veel te leren over supply chain, transport, data en optimalisatie.

Je krijgt veel vrijheid om te experimenteren, je eigen ideeën in te brengen en écht impact te maken op onze logistieke processen.

descriptionHtml:
🪐 Discover our galaxy Join the Future of Work ! Malt is Europe's leading freelance marketplace, connecting over 1,000,000 talented freelancers with 100,000+ companies. Founded in 2013, we're transforming how work gets done through our tech-powered, human-centered platform. What makes us different:
  • A diverse team of 600 Malters across 6 European countries
  • A culture that champions equality (50% of our Comex are women) and inclusive growth
  • Backed by top investors including ISAI, Serena Capital, Eurazeo Growth, Goldman Sachs, and BPI
  • A mission to give everyone the freedom to work differently
Ready to help shape the future of work? Your next chapter starts here! At Malt we believe that Ambition is the Way, so all lists of missions and responsibilities are non-exhaustive.
The Mission 🪐
  • The Situation: Malt is cementing its position as the undeniable leader in the European freelance economy. While our tech-powered platform connects over 1,000,000 top-tier freelancers with 100,000+ companies, the DACH Enterprise sector presents a massive, untapped frontier. This market is dominated by complex, multinational corporate structures with deeply entrenched procurement protocols that are ripe for disruption.
  • The Task: We are not hiring you to manage an existing portfolio or farm warm leads. You are being brought in to architect and own the zero-to-one enterprise acquisition strategy for the DACH region. Operating as the "founder" of your territory, your mandate is to systematically penetrate massive global accounts, navigate labyrinthine procurement structures, and secure highly scalable, multi-country Master Service Agreements (MSAs) that will cement Malt's dominance in the German-speaking market and beyond.

    • Key Responsibilities ✨

    Pillar 1: Strategic Territory Architecture & Hunting

  • Action: Map out complex, global enterprise accounts within the DACH region, aggressively designing and executing surgical prospecting strategies to breach heavily fortified multi-stakeholder environments (Procurement, HR, and independent Business Units).
  • Output: A localized, highly qualified pipeline of net-new DACH Enterprise logos and concrete, multi-threaded stakeholder maps.
  • Metrics of Performance: Enterprise GSV Pipeline Generated and CRM forecast integrity.

    • Pillar 2: Deal Orchestration & RFP Command

  • Action: Run rigorous, in-depth discovery utilizing the full MEDDIC framework to validate severe business pain, identify the true Economic Buyer, and aggressively lead end-to-end RFI/RFP processes alongside our Bid Management and technical teams.
  • Output: Compelling, ROI-driven business proposals and precisely engineered enterprise pilot programs designed to prove undeniable platform value.
  • Metrics of Performance: RFI/RFP Win Rate and Pilot-to-MSA Conversion Rate.

    • Pillar 3: Heavy-Weight Negotiation & Scalable Revenue Activation

  • Action: Command ruthless, complex negotiations for global Master Service Agreements involving tight friction with Legal, Finance, and Procurement across multiple countries. Upon signature, engineer the scalable handover strategy to the local Account Management teams.
  • Output: Executed, multi-country MSAs and comprehensive post-signature deployment kickoff plans.
  • Metrics of Performance: Total Contract Value (TCV) Signed and Deal Velocity (managing complex cycles efficiently without losing momentum).

    • Requirements & The Skills Matrix 🔍

    Proven Mastery (What you have already built):

  • A minimum of 8 years of quantifiable, proven track record hunting and closing complex, 7-figure B2B sales cycles within a SaaS/Tech environment.
  • Deep familiarity with the staffing, "future of work" industry, MSPs, or Tier 1 recruitment groups.
  • Demonstrated success navigating extremely long sales cycles and managing strategic concessions to close highly scalable deals.
  • Native-level fluency in German and full professional fluency in English.

    • Skills You Will Deploy & Develop:

  • Advanced MEDDIC Mastery: You will deploy this framework with such rigor that you act as the internal benchmark and can actively coach others on its nuances.
  • C-Suite ROI Narrative Construction: Mastering the art of delivering disruptive narratives that challenge legacy customer assumptions and shift C-level perspectives on the "Future of Work."
  • Cross-Border Deal Structuring: Developing top-tier acumen in multi-country legal, financial, and compliance orchestration.

    • The Self-Selection Filter ❓

    This role is perfect for you if:

  • You are an elite hunter who actively enjoys the strategic friction of a complex enterprise sales cycle and navigating massive corporate red tape.
  • You operate with extreme ownership—you treat your pipeline like your own startup's P&L and do not wait for permission or inbound leads to execute.
  • You naturally think in terms of "Economic Buyers," "Decision Criteria," and "Validation Events" rather than just "having good meetings."

    • This role is NOT for you if:

  • You rely heavily on inbound marketing or a pre-packaged SDR playbook to hit your pipeline numbers.
  • You get easily intimidated by heavy-weight legal negotiations, aggressive procurement teams, or highly structured RFP processes.
  • You prefer predictable, transactional account maintenance over the high-stakes thrill of net-new, multi-country enterprise acquisition.

    • 30-60-90 Day Impact Plan 🏁
  • Day 30: Submerge into our marketplace mechanics, master the Malt value proposition, and map the top tier of DACH global enterprise accounts. Output: Delivery of your fully architected account penetration strategy.
  • Day 60: Execute initial outreach, identify key Economic Buyers within target accounts, and begin orchestrating your first high-stakes pilot phases. Output: Establish a predictable, MEDDIC-qualified enterprise pipeline.
  • Day 90: Take absolute control of your Metrics of Performance. Lead your first complex RFI/RFP processes or MSA negotiations end-to-end and initiate scalable handover plans. Output: Secure early enterprise traction that directly impacts the regional bottom line.

    • How to join the mission? 🚀
  • First Call (45m): High-level alignment with Niko (Talent Acquisition Lead) to audit your background and entrepreneurial drive.
  • Strategic Deep Dive (60m): Interview with your future manager, Théo, to dissect your past enterprise deals and MEDDIC rigor.
  • Business Case (60m): A live simulation to assess your technical account development, localized prospecting skills, and C-level narrative delivery.
  • Final Vision Call (30m): Interview with our CRO to discuss Malt’s long-term scale and how your ambition aligns with our macro-economic growth.
    • Life on planet Malt is the perfect space to thrive personally and professionally 💫 🤝 Onboarding: Before easing into your new role, you’ll spend your first week learning about our culture, products, and services with other onboardees at our office in Paris. 💻 Remote work: Hybrid remote policy - 3 days office / 2 days home-office. 🏖️ Annual leave: 30 days/year. 📆 Sabbatical: 1 month paid sabbatical once you've been with Malt for 3 years. 📈 Stock options: Every Malter is entitled to stock options. 🍽️ Lunch vouchers:6,50€ per day / 15 days a month. 🐶 Dog friendly office: In the heart of Munich/Berlin! ❓ Choose your Benefit: Transport reimbursement, Gym membership, Organic Food voucher or Rydes Mobility App. 📚 Free books: If you’re interested in learning more about any topic relevant to Malt’s business, just tell us the books you’d like to read, and we’ll order them for you—without any questions asked or approval processes to follow. title: Supplier & Third Party Risk Manager
descriptionHtml:
Thought Machine's mission is bold – to properly and permanently rid the world's banks of legacy technology. To achieve this, we have developed the foundations of modern banking through core and payments technology which run natively in the cloud. What we are attempting is hard and means we need great people working together to build great technology.

We have grown rapidly in the past few years – growing our team to more than 550 individuals across offices in London, New York, Singapore, Sydney and our newly established Engineering Hub in Lisbon. We have raised more than £500m in funding and our investors include Molten Ventures, Eurazeo, Intesa Sanpaolo, Temasek, Nyca Partners, JPMorgan Chase Strategic Investments, Standard Chartered Ventures, and more.

We have created a culture that enables our team to produce the best work in the industry while ensuring we have fun along the way. We're regularly cited as having a fantastic workplace culture and have been recognised by Sifted magazine as having one of the highest Glassdoor ratings for a UK fintech company and the industry's most generous employee share package. Named one of the world's most innovative fintechs by Global Finance Magazine, we were also recognised by the Financial Times as one of Europe's fastest-growing companies for two consecutive years—and a UK Best Employer for 2026.

About Thought Machine

Thought Machine is building the future of banking. Our cloud-native core banking platform, Vault, and our payments platform are used by some of the world's largest banks to modernise their technology and launch new products quickly and safely. Because our clients are regulated financial institutions, the way we select, manage and oversee our own suppliers matters to them as much as it does to us.

About the team

The Risk & Compliance team sits within Finance and is responsible for enterprise risk management, the internal controls framework, regulatory compliance, external certifications (including SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 22301 and PCI DSS), client audits and third-party risk management and procurement. We are a small, high-impact team that works across the whole business, from Sales and Engineering to Security, Legal and the Board.

About the role

The Supplier & Third Party Risk Manager will take end-to-end ownership of our third-party vendor ecosystem. Using our procurement platform (Omnea), you will lead commercial negotiations, proactively manage contract renewals, and establish a robust Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) programme to safeguard the company against commercial, operational, regulatory and security risk. This is a builder role: we have the tooling and the onboarding process in place, and we are looking for someone to turn it into a mature procurement and supplier management capability that delivers measurable cost savings and better outcomes from our suppliers.

What you will do

Establish and lead the TPRM programme

  • Expand and maintain the enterprise-wide Third-Party Risk Management policy and framework.

  • Partner closely with InfoSec, Legal, Compliance and the Data Protection Officer to build standardised due diligence workflows, and maintain an active third-party risk register.

  • Ensure our supplier oversight meets the expectations of our regulated banking clients and supports our external certifications and client audits.

Proactive renewals management

  • Take full ownership of the global contract renewal calendar.

  • Partner with budget holders and FP&A well in advance of notice periods to assess supplier performance, review actual usage and ROI, and renegotiate terms or terminate contracts to eliminate unwanted auto-renewals.

Strategic sourcing and negotiation

  • Support commercial negotiations for software, professional services, contractors and corporate overheads to optimise commercial terms and Total Cost of Ownership (TCO).

  • Identify consolidation opportunities across enterprise-wide software spend and track savings delivered.

System ownership and process automation

  • Act as the primary business owner for Omnea.

  • Use the platform to automate intake requests, route conditional security risk assessments, track contract approvals, and maintain a centralised repository of active suppliers.

Vendor governance and performance

  • Design and implement a structured vendor governance framework.

  • Segment the supplier portfolio by criticality and establish ongoing monitoring (SLAs / KPIs) for high-risk and critical vendors.

  • Produce regular reporting on supplier performance, risk and spend for senior management.

Business partnership

  • Act as a commercial partner and advisor to department leaders across the business to support their purchasing needs, helping them navigate onboarding smoothly.

What we are looking for

Essential

  • 3–6 years' experience in Procurement, Sourcing or Vendor Risk Management, ideally within a high-growth scaleup, regulated fintech or fast-paced financial services environment.

  • Practical experience running third-party risk assessments, with an understanding of fundamental security and data privacy standards (e.g. ISO 27001, SOC 2 and GDPR).

  • A track record of managing contract lifecycles, identifying consolidation opportunities, and using usage data to negotiate better renewal terms.

  • Good negotiation skills with a track record of delivering cost savings and driving value from suppliers.

  • A proactive, builder mindset, with the ability to design processes and establish strong internal relationships.

Desirable

  • Experience with modern spend management and procurement orchestration platforms (direct experience with Omnea or similar tools is highly advantageous).

  • Familiarity with regulatory expectations on outsourcing and third-party risk in financial services (e.g. DORA, EBA outsourcing guidelines, PRA SS2/21).

  • A relevant qualification or progress towards one (e.g. CIPS).

We actively hire candidates who demonstrate technical excellence in their field and welcome people of all ages and backgrounds, providing everyone with equal access to professional development. You are encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't accurately match the job description. We also encourage applications from those with different abilities, including candidates with ADHD, autism, dyslexia or dyspraxia.

title: SVP Industrial (all genders)
descriptionHtml:
Your Mission:

As SVP Industrial (all genders), you will lead VÆRIDION’s existing programme and industrial teams through one of the company’s most important milestones: the build and delivery of the first conforming Microliner prototype. Building on the aircraft programme, engineering definition, internal manufacturing capabilities, supplier network, and build preparation already in place, you will integrate and lead the industrial effort required to turn the design into complete, certifiable hardware. You will own integrated industrial delivery across build strategy, manufacturing planning, tooling, infrastructure, supplier and material readiness, shop-floor execution, configuration control, conformity, quality, and resolution of build issues. In parallel, you will strengthen the industrial system and organisation that carries the Microliner from the first conforming aircraft through the remaining certification aircraft, low-rate initial production, and scalable series production. As a member of the senior leadership team, you will shape company-wide operational decisions and have the potential to grow into the COO role as VÆRIDION scales.

 

Your Day-to-Day:

  • Lead VÆRIDION’s industrial organisation through the build and delivery of the first conforming Microliner prototype as the role’s immediate and highest-priority mission, taking integrated accountability for industrial planning, build readiness, execution, schedule, quality, cost, and successful completion of the aircraft.

  • Build and lead the industrial organisation across Prototype Manufacturing, Manufacturing Engineering, Production Operations, industrial infrastructure, tooling and automation, production planning and control, logistics, and warehouse operations.

  • Translate the aircraft design and certification basis into a manufacturable, inspectable, and repeatable production system, embedding Design for Manufacture and Assembly from an early stage.

  • Establish the factory concept, make-or-buy architecture, production flow, capacity model, workplace design, and capital expenditure plan required to meet programme milestones and target unit economics.

  • Bring together and lead the integrated build organisation for the first conforming prototype, aligning the established work of Prototype Manufacturing, Manufacturing Engineering, Production Operations, Quality, Engineering, Procurement, and suppliers. Own the integrated build sequence, work packages, material and supplier readiness, work instructions, tooling, jigs, fixtures, equipment qualification, operator readiness, daily build control, issue resolution, configuration discipline, and the structured transfer of learning into subsequent aircraft and the production system.

  • Lead the establishment and approval of VÆRIDION’s Production Organisation under EASA Part-21 Subpart G (POA), including the production organisation exposition, accountable governance, nominated functions, procedures, competence framework, independent quality assurance, supplier control, production conformity, and coordination with the competent authority.

  • Drive production quality, configuration discipline, traceability, non-conformance management, and continuous improvement in close cooperation with Quality, Engineering, and Certification.

  • Create and manage the integrated industrial plan, including build schedules, resource and capacity planning, critical-path management, industrial risk, and recovery actions.

  • Develop the industrial supplier interface with Procurement and Engineering, ensuring suppliers can meet technical maturity, quality, capacity, cost, and delivery requirements.

  • Establish industrial KPIs and management routines covering safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, inventory, and ramp-up maturity.

  • Recruit, develop, and lead a high-performing, hands-on team while building a culture of ownership, disciplined execution, practical problem-solving, and aviation-grade safety and quality.

  • Represent Industrial in company, programme, and leadership reviews and provide clear recommendations on industrial trade-offs, investment decisions, organisational priorities, risks, and readiness.

 

Your Profile:

  • Degree in aerospace, mechanical, industrial, manufacturing, production engineering, or a comparable technical discipline.

  • Typically 15+ years of relevant experience in aerospace or another highly regulated, safety-critical product environment, including substantial senior leadership responsibility across prototype manufacturing, industrialisation, manufacturing engineering, or production operations.

  • Demonstrated experience leading the successful build and delivery of a first-of-type or initial conforming prototype in aerospace or another complex, safety-critical hardware environment, with direct accountability for cross-functional build execution, configuration, quality, schedule, supplier readiness, and resolution of first-build issues. Experience carrying those lessons into certification aircraft, industrialisation, and low-rate initial production is highly valued.

  • Strong command of industrial engineering methods, production-system design, capacity and resource planning, tooling and equipment industrialisation, production planning and control, and operational performance management.

  • Working knowledge of aerospace production and quality requirements, including configuration control, traceability, non-conformance and corrective-action processes, production readiness, and the interaction between design, certification, quality, and manufacturing.

  • Strong practical knowledge of EASA Part-21 Subpart G and experience establishing, significantly scaling, or holding senior responsibility within a Production Organisation Approval; first-hand involvement in a new POA application is highly valued.

  • Commercial judgement and experience building industrial business cases, make-or-buy decisions, investment plans, cost models, and supplier industrial-readiness assessments.

  • A pragmatic, hands-on leadership style: comfortable moving between strategic architecture, detailed factory and build issues, and direct support to teams on the shop floor.

  • Strong cross-functional leadership, structured problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to create clarity and accountability in a fast-moving scale-up environment.

  • Excellent written and spoken English. German is beneficial but not required.

We recognize that women and other under-represented groups are often overlooked in our industry. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every listed qualification, we still encourage you to apply. Talent and potential can’t always be captured in a checklist.

 

Why us?

  • Virtual stock options: Participate in VÆRIDION’s long-term success through our VSOP.

  • EGYM Wellpass: Subsidized membership to support your physical and mental wellbeing.

  • Family leave: 10 days of family leave following the birth of your child.

  • Office Culture: We’re an in-office company with flexibility around working hours, occasional remote work and personal commitments.

  • Room to grow: Take ownership of your work, bring your own ideas and develop through independent projects.

  • Shape the future of aviation: Work with an ambitious team building the next generation of electric aviation.

VÆRIDION was founded in 2021 to transform regional air travel with the Microliner, a 100% electric commercial aircraft. By delivering the most energy-efficient aircraft, we are building the future where clean, safe, and affordable electric aviation seamlessly connects people and businesses. We’re bringing together the brightest minds in aerospace, automotive engineering, and business to disrupt the aviation industry.

title: Technical Programme Manager, Security Engineering (Risk)
descriptionHtml:
About the AI Security Institute

The AI Security Institute is the world's largest and best-funded team dedicated to understanding advanced AI risks and translating that knowledge into action. We’re in the heart of the UK government with direct lines to No. 10 (the Prime Minister's office), and we work with frontier developers and governments globally.

We’re here because governments are critical for advanced AI going well, and UK AISI is uniquely positioned to mobilise them. With our resources, unique agility and international influence, this is the best place to shape both AI development and government action.

The deadline for applying to this role is Wednesday 25th November 2026, end of day (UK Time).

About the team

As the models we test get more capable and the environments we run them in get more sensitive, we have to continue to be able to run evaluations of highly capable models under proper control and ensure that it remains governed well. Building that governance and keeping it fast is what lets AISI keep pace with the work in front of it.

The Security Engineering team keeps AISI's research platform, evaluation environments, and sensitive data secure, and runs the governance, risk, and compliance around them. We harden the environments evaluations run in, detect and respond to threats, and build the controls that let evaluations of highly capable models proceed safely. We work with research teams across AISI, with partners in frontier AI companies and government.

About the role

Rigorous safety governance and fast-moving research aren't mutually exclusive. AISI research involves working with highly capable AI models, often before they have been released to the public and often with lowered safeguards, to understand their true capabilities. That work has to be properly controlled, and someone has to build the processes and systems that help us make the call that it's safe to run without becoming a bottleneck. We're hiring a Technical Programme Manager in Security Engineering to own the AISI-wide governance mechanism that oversees these safety judgements, the controls research teams work under, and every edge case and escalation in between. You'll work with the team's engineers and the researchers whose work this governs.

What you'll own:

  • AISI-wide Governance Mechanism that oversees safety. Own the process, make clear what it approves and how, help people work through their requirements proactively, and keep decisions well-evidenced and moving.
  • The research/control interface. You'll own how research teams meet the security controls that apply to their work, and the defined path for handling the exceptions.
  • Programme architecture and delivery. You'll track the team's work and spot problems early, with enough visibility to stay in control.
  • Cross-government governance engagement. You'll represent AISI on governance and risk with partners across government, including the Cabinet Office, building the relationships, and turning departmental policy into AISI process.

Who we're looking for

Essential experience:

You may be a good fit if you have some of the following skills, experience and attitudes:

  • A track record with technical colleagues. You've delivered technical programmes somewhere similarly ambiguous. You can scope and structure an open-ended goal. Technical teams trust you.
  • Comfort at the frontier of AI. You don't have to be an ML researcher, but you need to hold your own in constant conversation with technical staff about the work, the strategy, and the risks. You should have a view on what's hard, what's speculative, what's blocked, and what "good" looks like.
  • High agency and ownership. You own outcomes, not activity.
  • Strong prioritisation under pressure. You can tell what actually matters day to day and quarter to quarter.

Desirable experience:

Strong candidates may also have:

  • Experience in security, risk, or GRC. A technical background with a genuine interest in security is ideal but not required.
  • Fluency in, or appetite for, modern productivity tools (coding agents, Linear, Slack) and AI tools as part of daily work.

We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every point above. We care more about what you've broken, and how, than about certifications or job titles.

Selection process 

The interview process may vary from vacancy to vacancy, however, you should expect a typical process to include some technical proficiency tests, discussions with a cross-section of our team at AISI (including non-technical staff) and conversations with your team lead. The process will culminate in a conversation with members of the senior leadership team here at AISI.     

Candidates should expect to go through some or all of the following stages once an application has been submitted:   

  • Application - CV and a short cover note (max 500 words) explaining what draws you to this role and what you would bring.
  • Screening interview - Lightweight conversation on trajectory, motivation and fit.  
  • Work test - A take-home exercise designed to test programme management judgement in context. You will receive this after the screening interview. 
  • Technical interview - Discussion of your work test. 
  • Behavioural interview - Deeper dive on stakeholder management, prioritisation and team dynamics. 
  • Senior leadership interview (30 min) - Final conversation with AISI senior leadership.  

Security Clearance

Appointment is conditional on successfully completing UK Government SC clearance. Prior clearance is not required—we will sponsor and support you. You should normally have been resident in the UK for the past 5 years. More detail on clearance eligibility can be found on the UK Government website: National security vetting: clearance levels - GOV.UK.   

What We Offer 

Impact you couldn't have anywhere else 

  • Incredibly talented, mission-driven and supportive colleagues. 
  • Direct influence on how frontier AI is governed and deployed globally. 
  • Work with the Prime Minister’s AI Advisor and leading AI companies. 
  • Opportunity to shape the first & best-resourced public-interest research team focused on AI security. 

Resources & access 

  • Pre-release access to multiple frontier models and ample compute. 
  • Extensive operational support so you can focus on research and ship quickly. 
  • Work with experts across national security, policy, AI research and adjacent sciences. 

Growth & autonomy 

  • If you’re talented and driven, you’ll own important problems early. 
  • 5 days off and annual stipends for learning and development, and funding for conferences and external collaborations. 
  • Freedom to pursue research bets without product pressure. 
  • Opportunities to publish and collaborate externally. 

Life & family* 

  • Modern central London office, or where applicable, option to work in similar government offices in Birmingham, Cardiff, Darlington, Edinburgh, Salford or Bristol. 
  • Hybrid working, flexibility for occasional remote work abroad and stipends for work-from-home equipment. 
  • At least 25 days’ annual leave, 8 public holidays, extra team-wide breaks and 3 days off for volunteering. 
  • Generous paid parental leave (36 weeks of UK statutory leave shared between parents + 3 extra paid weeks + option for additional unpaid time). 
  • Excellent pension provision, with a choice between Partnership (no employee contributions required and up to 14.75% employer contributions) or Alpha, a valuable defined benefit scheme that provides a guaranteed, inflation-linked retirement income for life. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).
  • Discounts and benefits for cycling to work, donations and retail/gyms. 
     

*These benefits apply to direct employees. Benefits may differ for individuals joining through other employment arrangements such as secondments. 

Salary

Annual salary is benchmarked to role scope and relevant experience. Most offers land between £65,000 and £145,000 made up of a base salary plus a technical allowance (take-home salary = base + technical allowance). 

This role sits outside of the DDaT pay framework given the scope of this role requires in depth technical expertise in frontier AI safety, robustness and advanced AI architectures. 

The full range of salaries are available below: 

  • Level 3: £65,000–£75,000 (Base £40,850 + Technical Allowance £24,150–£34,150)
  • Level 4: £85,000–£95,000 (Base £48,540 + Technical Allowance £36,460–£46,460)
  • Level 5: £105,000–£115,000 (Base £63,165 + Technical Allowance £41,835–£51,835)
  • Level 6: £125,000–£135,000 (Base £76,475 + Technical Allowance £48,525–£58,525)
  • Level 7: £145,000 (Base £76,475 + Technical Allowance £68,525)

Additional Information

Use of AI in Applications

Artificial Intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Use of AI tools in recruitment

We may use AI tools to help our hiring team review applications, for example by summarising application materials and helping us prioritise them against the published criteria. We do not use AI tools to find information about you from other sources, including online. People make every decision. We do not make solely automated decisions about candidates. Find out more, including your rights, in our recruitment privacy notice: https://www.aisi.gov.uk/careers/privacy-policy.

Internal Fraud Database 

The Internal Fraud function of the Fraud, Error, Debt and Grants Function at the Cabinet Office processes details of civil servants who have been dismissed for committing internal fraud, or who would have been dismissed had they not resigned. The Cabinet Office receives the details from participating government organisations of civil servants who have been dismissed, or who would have been dismissed had they not resigned, for internal fraud. In instances such as this, civil servants are then banned for 5 years from further employment in the civil service. The Cabinet Office then processes this data and discloses a limited dataset back to DLUHC as a participating government organisations. DLUHC then carry out the pre employment checks so as to detect instances where known fraudsters are attempting to reapply for roles in the civil service. In this way, the policy is ensured and the repetition of internal fraud is prevented.  For more information please see - Internal Fraud Register.

Security

Successful candidates must undergo a criminal record check and get baseline personnel security standard (BPSS) clearance before they can be appointed. Additionally, there is a strong preference for eligibility for counter-terrorist check (CTC) clearance. Some roles may require higher levels of clearance, and we will state this by exception in the job advertisement. See our vetting charter here.

Nationality requirements

We may be able to offer roles to applicant from any nationality or background. As such we encourage you to apply even if you do not meet the standard nationality requirements (opens in a new window).

title: Technical Project Manager - Dach (m/f/d)
descriptionHtml:
Build something monumental for Healthcare!

At Tandem Health we’re reimagining healthcare by putting clinicians first. Our platform - designed by clinicians, for clinicians - is built on deep insight into real-world pain points, with intuitive medical notes and workflows that truly support patient care.

We’re a fast-scaling health-tech company backed by top investors and expanding globally. We move fast, stay curious, and believe building something that matters starts with an extraordinary team. If you're passionate about impact and innovation, we'd love to meet you!

About the Role

You care about making complex systems actually work, not just in theory, but in practice - across teams, stakeholders, and real-world constraints. In previous roles, you were likely the person who brought clarity to messy situations: aligning engineers, partners, and product teams to get things shipped.

At Tandem, you'll drive how our platform connects with the external systems used across French and European healthcare - owning and driving some of the most critical technical initiatives we have. You'll be based in our Munich office, working alongside the local team, in close collaboration with our central Integrations team in Stockholm. A big part of the role is deeply understanding both sides: the capabilities and constraints of external systems, and those of our own platform. From that understanding, you'll find ways to integrate them and shape concrete proposals for how integrations should work, together with external partners.

You move fast, but not carelessly. You know how to break down complex problems, prioritize what matters, and keep momentum across multiple workstreams. You're comfortable going deep technically when needed, understanding APIs, data flows, and system constraints, while still keeping the bigger product picture in mind.


This is a high-impact role where you'll not only deliver projects, but shape how we build and scale technical products at Tandem.


What You'll Do

  • Lead integration work with external partners and healthcare systems, ensuring high-quality, scalable implementations.

  • Map external systems against our own platform and propose concrete integration designs to external partners.

  • Act as the central point of coordination between engineering, partnerships, and external stakeholders, bridging the local team in Germany and the integrations team in Stockholm.

  • Translate complex technical requirements into clear priorities, plans, and deliverables.

  • Work closely with engineers to understand APIs, data models, and system architecture, and ensure solutions are robust and aligned with our platform.

  • Identify bottlenecks, manage dependencies, and keep projects moving at high velocity.

  • Build and improve how we work - establishing processes, templates, and frameworks for integrations and technical delivery.

  • Ensure strong visibility across stakeholders - tracking progress, surfacing risks, and communicating clearly.

  • Support our sales organisation in answering technical questions from our customers.

     

What You Bring

  • Experience as a Technical Project Manager or similar role in a SaaS, platform, or healthtech environment.

  • Strong ability to drive complex, cross-functional initiatives involving both internal teams and external stakeholders.

  • Technical fluency - comfortable discussing APIs, authentication, integrations, and system design with engineers.

  • Proven ability to manage multiple workstreams without losing clarity or momentum.

  • Ability to anticipate, assess, and manage risk in projects, from scoping through to delivery.

  • Strong communication skills, you can translate technical complexity into clear decisions and direction.

  • A product mindset - you care about building the right thing, not just delivering on time.

  • Native level german speaking.

Bonus Points

  • Experience in tech sales, enterprise sales, or enterprise software delivery

  • Experience working with healthcare systems or regulated environments

  • Familiarity with FHIR, HL7, or other healthcare data standards

  • Experience working with platform or API products

  • Some hands-on technical experience (e.g. scripting, debugging, light coding)

  • Experience scaling integration processes or working with multiple external partners

Location

We believe the best ideas happen when we're together. This role is based in our Munich office, where you will work primarily on-site with the local team, while collaborating closely with colleagues at our HQ in Stockholm.

 

How to Apply

We adopt a continuous selection process, so please make sure to apply with your CV in English.

Our interview process consists of 4 stages:

  • Screening interview with Talent Acquisition

  • Technical interview with some of our Engineering team

  • Follow-up interview with one of our Team Leads

  • Home case and presentation at our Munich office - Join us for a lunch, a discovery meeting and a presentation to experience our culture firsthand, collaborate with our team, and see how you work in action.

 

Culture at Tandem

At Tandem, we move fast, think big, and take ownership. We're a high-performing, diverse team with a shared drive to change the future of healthcare - and we’re just getting started.

Our culture is built on action, ambition, and learning. You'll be trusted to take the lead, challenge yourself, and make an impact from day one. We believe real growth happens when you're stretched, supported, and surrounded by smart, passionate teammates who want to win together.

Even though we’re spread across countries, we come together often in Sweden for team meetings, social events, and offsites - blending global reach with real human connection.

We hire for talent, potential, and attitude - valuing different backgrounds and fresh perspectives. Great ideas come from everywhere, and we’re building a team that reflects the world we want to change.

Tandem handles sensitive patient data and will conduct a background check before hiring any candidate.

title: Technical Support Engineer (L2) - Compute
descriptionHtml:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

Mistral AI is building a new Compute Support team to ensure the reliability, performance, and scalability of our GPU clusters in a Kubernetes environment. As one of the founding members of this team, you will play a pivotal role in shaping its processes, standards, and culture.

In this hybrid L1/L2 support role, you will be the first point of contact for customers and internal teams, providing technical guidance, troubleshooting, and issue resolution for compute-related inquiries. You’ll also serve as the escalation point for complex issues, leveraging your deep systems knowledge, Kubernetes expertise, and operational debugging skills to ensure our AI workloads run smoothly at scale.

This is a support-focused role that blends system administration, customer-facing communication, and compute infrastructure expertise. While coding is not the primary focus, familiarity with Go for debugging and automation is a plus.

  

Key Responsibilities

First Customer’s Point of Contact

  • Act as the first interlocutor for customers and internal teams, providing timely and effective responses to compute-related inquiries.

  • Triage and prioritize incoming requests, ensuring SLAs are met for acknowledgment, first response, and resolution.

  • Gather and analyze initial issue details (e.g., logs, error messages, system metrics) to diagnose problems efficiently.

  • Provide clear, actionable guidance to customers and internal users, including temporary workarounds where applicable.

  

Technical Support

  • Serve as the L2 escalation point for Linux, Kubernetes, and compute infrastructure issues, providing deep technical troubleshooting for:

    • GPU/TPU workloads (e.g., CUDA errors, memory leaks, job failures).

    • Kubernetes clusters (e.g., pod crashes, node failures, networking misconfigurations).

    • Bare metal and cloud environments (e.g., AWS EC2, GCP VMs, HPC clusters).

  • Diagnose and resolve performance bottlenecks, hardware failures, and resource contention in distributed systems.

  • Analyze system metrics, logs, and traces (e.g., dmesg, journalctl, nvidia-smi, Prometheus, Grafana) to identify root causes of issues.

  • Participate in on-call rotations to provide 24/7 support for critical compute systems

  • Nice to have: Optimize system configurations (e.g., kernel parameters, filesystem tuning, network settings) for high-performance computing (HPC) and AI workloads.

  

Kubernetes & Containerization

  • Debug Kubernetes clusters with a focus on:

    • Pod and node issues (e.g., CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled, ImagePullBackOff).

    • Networking and storage (e.g., CNI plugins, PersistentVolumes, StorageClasses).

    • Resource management (e.g., Requests/Limits, QOS classes, node affinity).

  • Troubleshoot container runtime issues (Docker, containerd) such as image pull failures, OCI compliance, or runtime errors.

  • Collaborate with SRE teams to understand and improve existing IaC (Terraform, Ansible) and Go-based tooling.

  

Documentation & Process Improvement

  • Create and maintain runbooks, playbooks, and internal documentation for common compute issues (e.g., GPU debugging, Kubernetes troubleshooting).

  • Contribute to post-mortems with actionable follow-ups to prevent recurring incidents.

  • Train internal teams on best practices for compute infrastructure and debugging.

  • Help define and refine support processes as a founding member of the new Compute Support team.

What We’re Looking For

Required Skills & Experience

  • 5+ years of experience in system administration, technical support, or infrastructure operations, with a strong focus on compute-heavy environments (bare metal, cloud, HPC, or virtualization).

  • Deep Linux/Unix expertise:

    • Debugging kernel-level issues (e.g., OOM killer, I/O bottlenecks, CPU throttling).

    • Performance tuning (e.g., sysctl, ulimit, filesystem optimizations).

    • Networking troubleshooting (e.g., iptables, tcpdump, DNS, NFS, SSH).

    • Storage management (e.g., LVM, RAID, NVMe, GPU-local storage).

  • Hands-on Kubernetes experience is mandatory:

    • Debugging pods, nodes, and clusters (e.g., kubectl describe, kubectl logs, crictl).

    • Networking and storage (e.g., CNI plugins, PersistentVolumes).

    • Resource management (e.g., Requests/Limits, QOS classes).

  • Familiarity with containerization (Docker, containerd) and basic IaC awareness Proficiency with monitoring tools (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, OpenTelemetry).

  • Basic scripting/automation skills (preferably Go, but Bash or Python are acceptable for ad-hoc tasks).

  • Experience with bare metal, virtualization, or HPC environments (e.g., Fluidstack, Coreweave, Vast) is a strong plus.

  • Excellent problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to explain technical issues clearly and patiently to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Customer-focused mindset with a passion for resolving issues efficiently and improving system reliability.

  • Ability to work in on-call rotations and handle high-pressure situations with a structured, calm approach.

  • Commitment to meeting tight SLAs for issue acknowledgment, triage, and first response.

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.
